in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the contribution of volunteering to european social cohesion, but i would like to make some financial and budgetary clarifications. the european union has launched the european voluntary service under the youth in action programme. it enables young people to undertake apprenticeships in various professions or work with non-governmental organisations in another member state. the operators of this service are companies and ngos accredited by the european commission in each member state. the budget of the european voluntary service is problematic, however. this is a sum of not more than eur 42 million per year, which should finance the travel costs of several tens of thousands of european volunteers, as well as other minimum related expenses. the interest from young people is very high, and there are many organizations that want to implement this program. in romania alone, a new member state, there are over 60 accredited organisations for volunteer exchange and over 5000 applications for such placements. although it has proved to be a highly attractive programme, the european voluntary service continues to be inadequately funded.
in writing. according to eurostat, in 2007, real prices of agricultural products in the union increased by 5% compared with 2006, the highest increase being recorded in romania (15.8%). in europe, the price increase for both milk and poultrymeat was 7.8%, with the highest price increases for crops being recorded for cereals (45.4%) and forage products (11.5%). again, romania recorded the highest increase (29.2%). last year in europe, the producer price of agricultural products increased by 4.6%, while producer costs increased by 5.3% and the level of subsidies decreased by 3.1%. in the new member states, the costs of farmers have risen very much and subsidies are very low. the largest declines in income per farmer were recorded in bulgaria (-18.6%) and romania (-16.1%). the low value, non-payment of agricultural subsidies and difficult access to credit for agriculture made it impossible to apply cropping technologies, thus achieving very low yields per hectare. competition for agricultural land use is also contributing to the rise in food prices, with the area under biofuel crops increasing by 13.6% in 2007 compared to 2006, and by 31.5% compared to 2002-06.
in writing. the latest developments in global agricultural markets are creating a situation that few governments are prepared to deal with. dramatic price increases, especially for basic grains, risk pushing millions of people into hunger. this new reality must be addressed by governments and the european institutions. the new level of agricultural prices presents new opportunities for producers, including those in eu countries. in romania, 40% of the population lives in rural areas, many of whom are agricultural producers. the new realities of agricultural markets present a chance for farmers to improve their economic performance and, by implication, their standard of living. unfortunately, the agricultural segment reacts very heavily to price changes in world markets. small producers face a stiff bureaucracy and are at a disadvantage in negotiating procurement contracts with large, dominant retail chains. the eu must support small farmers so that they can benefit from higher incomes from their labour. market access for small farmers must be facilitated and global distributors must be subject to transparent regulations that prevent anti-competitive policies.
the legislation we are discussing today has the potential to improve the lives of more than a million european citizens working in another member state as service providers or posted workers. in particular, the provisions of article 3 of the directive are not fully implemented in every member state of the european union. the health and safety standards, the maximum number of hours of work and minimum leave periods or the maternity protection measures do not apply to posted workers. at the same time, the minimum wage laid down by the legislation of the host state must be guaranteed. this last aspect, however, leads many firms to resort to alternative employment contracts, which automatically prevent lower wages. in addition, it has become a practice for many european firms to hire workers from the new member states and send them abroad as posted workers for a period that can be extended up to 24 months, thus taking advantage of the differences in social security contributions. i conclude by saying that this kind of social dumping must be stopped by implementing all the provisions of the posting of workers directive.
madam president, i congratulate my colleague ms ana gomes for her work and her comprehensive and realistic assessments. as the report shows, china is already an important economic and political partner for africa. regarding africa’s development, i believe that there is so much work to do on this continent and that china, as a new player, should be welcome to participate. however, what i strongly fear is that instead of channelling its support in constructive endeavours – health, education, poverty reduction and infrastructure – china would continue to engage in feeding the tragedies of the continent and will do it by arms trafficking and undermining whatever steps african countries make towards democracy, good governance and respect for human rights. the chinese ship carrying guns for zimbabwe again calls into question china’s real commitment to contributing to peace and security in africa. many african countries welcome their cooperation with china as there is no political conditionality linked to the economic benefits, but the eu should continue to strongly advocate, both to china and the african countries, institution building, human rights advancement and more transparent rules regarding the exploitation of natural resources. recent developments have shown that, even in those cases where in the last couple of years governments started to show more openness on how public money and resources were spent, they have gone back to a less transparent administration. the eu has the duty to help china to become a trusted partner in development cooperation.
the value of china's trade with africa increased from eur 2 billion in 1999 to approximately eur 39.7 billion in 2005, and china is now africa's third largest trading partner. this very clearly demonstrates the major interest that africa represents for china's global interests. the resolution has some very important conclusions which deserve to be stressed once again. we have to make it very clear that our expectation is that china's involvement in africa is not just about the nations that are of interest from the point of view of energy policy. we should also encourage china to provide unconditional assistance to african partners, and that the economic conditions attached to international subsidies or loans do not undermine the objective of sustainable development. it is more important for us to see what we are going to do, what the european union is going to do in this situation. i agree with commissioner louis michel when he said that unfortunately the european union is not taking advantage of its unique position in africa. the european union needs to redirect a larger part of its current budget for financial support to infrastructure projects that have the capacity to attract foreign direct investment. finally, a stronger european presence in africa must be transformed from a wish into a reality.
mr president, i think that human rights and women’s rights should also be a high priority in the relationship between the european union and latin america. i would like to draw your attention to a specific situation in nicaragua. the ban on therapeutic abortion, which was legally imposed in 2006, has already had tragic consequences on women’s health, with all victims of rape, such as a nine-year-old girl or a paraplegic twelve-year-old girl, obliged to go through with their pregnancies although their own lives are at stake. moreover, lawyers and human rights defenders are themselves under criminal investigation for incitement to commit crimes, merely because they challenge this inhuman legislation or because they defend doctors. this is unacceptable and the european union cannot afford to be silent. last week, the parliamentary assembly of the council of europe adopted a resolution on access to safe and legal abortion in europe, which means that we care about women in europe. but, if we want to convince our citizens that human rights are values that we genuinely treasure, we must prove that we do not apply double standards with regard to partners with whom agreements negotiations are ongoing.

mr president, for me it is obvious that the eu still has no say in the negotiations with the us. the twin-track approach is just proof of the council and commission’s failure to protect european interests and citizens. the fact that member states are left alone to negotiate bilaterally with the us undermines our credibility and strength on the international scene and it might be to the detriment of our citizens whose data might be exchanged without any democratic scrutiny. i believe that member states should act in a european framework and i want the commission to show determination and make our us partner understand that equal rights and equal treatment are not negotiable. the etas that will be put in place could be a positive evolution as entry applications would be evaluated on the basis of each individual and not according to the country of origin. this would be a first step for equal treatment. no matter the nationality, we have to make europe without internal borders a reality and ensure equal treatment for all europeans.
the european commission now has increased negotiating power following the mandate given last week by the member states' interior ministers. in addition, we come after a series of productive meetings with the us representatives, the latest of which was the eu-us troika on justice and home affairs on 13 march. i believe that the three principles adopted on that occasion should be emphasised as much as possible, in particular the common objective of eliminating visas as quickly as possible. despite significant progress, rejection rates in some member states continue to rise. in romania it reached 37 percent, almost 10 percent more than the previous year, even though our country has meanwhile become a member of the european union. this development unfortunately takes us further away from the 10% target set in the visa weaver programme. at present, only concerted action by all member states can resolve this issue of visa reciprocity between the european union and the usa. we must ensure that by the next eu-us summit, our position is uniform and unwavering towards visa liberalisation for all european citizens, based on a very well-established timetable.
mr president, the intention of both the council and the commission in stressing their determination to negotiate with the us on the removal of visas on behalf of all european citizens, as well as the preparatory technical steps to be taken to that effect, are commendable. however, a gap has already appeared between the multilateral negotiations the eu is preparing to initiate, which is likely to take time, and the concrete results already obtained by some eu countries through bilateral negotiations with the us. after all, we are all aiming for the same result – the elimination of visas for travelling to the us. it is just that we are confronted with an option – either to wait for the multilateral negotiations between the eu and the us to take off and get it later, or to enter bilateral negotiations with the us and get it much sooner. to force the eu member countries to choose the less attractive option for the sake of a false solidarity, which is not respected by many eu member countries with regard to other, much important matters – like energy for instance – is at least morally wrong, all the more so since half of european citizens are already exempted from visa requirements through earlier bilateral negotations with the us.
i believe that there is a special status relationship between the european union and the united states. most member states are part of nato and participate jointly in ensuring security in europe and other countries when needed, without any differences between them. however, there are differences in the granting of visas to the united states, which are based on criteria that are not sufficiently clear and transparent at this time. the main criterion, under 10% of visa refusals, is a criterion that depends exclusively on the us authorities and not on the citizens applying for visas. the european institutions have so far failed to conclude negotiations to the benefit of european citizens. this has led to each member state seeking independent ways to resolve the situation. it is a good thing that these negotiations have intensified recently and that they can be conducted in parallel by the european union and the member states. it is imperative that one of the negotiated topics be the criteria for granting visas. only clear and, above all, transparent criteria will make the necessary information available to citizens before they apply for visas.
romania is among the european union member states whose citizens require a visa to enter the united states. contrary to the actions of other member states, romania has so far avoided engaging in effective bilateral negotiations with the united states, although its partnership with the united states and the presence of romanian troops in iraq and afghanistan would have allowed it to invoke bilateral solutions to the visa problem. i support a common approach of the eu member states and a mandate to the european commission to quickly identify a solution for visa exemption in the united states for citizens of the european union, including romanians. a real, consistent and effective negotiating effort is needed from the european commission. otherwise, in the last resort, against the backdrop of pressure from the romanian public opinion, which cannot be ignored, romania will have to find a quick solution through bilateral negotiations with the united states, just like other eu member states that have solved their american visa problem, disregarding the common position of brussels. finally, i regret the absence from the debate of mr frattini, who would have had the duty to fight for fair treatment and free movement for european and romanian citizens and not to promote discriminatory policies for romanian citizens, community citizens living and working in italy, most of whom are properly integrated into italian society.

the chairman of the council. − it was extremely interesting to be present at this dynamic debate. i think it was conducted in conditions where we all know one thing: legal migration is one thing. these are the ones the european union needs, legal migration. the second is illegal migration, and these are the ones that need to be fought, and these are the ones that are the subject of today's debate, that are on the agenda of today's debate. certainly the presidency is one of those who believe that illegal migration is a phenomenon that must be fought because they usually have a criminal background, they are backed by organised crime companies, and they don't care much about what people go through trying to get them into the european union in this case. i must say that i do not agree with those honourable members who feel that the council is avoiding this debate. i also cannot agree with those who think we are still only talking. the council is not avoiding this debate. it was the slovenian presidency that organised the conference on the future challenges of the management of the external borders of the european union in march this year, and all or most of the issues raised in today's debate were discussed at this conference, and this conference was held at ministerial level. i certainly agree with mrs hennis-plasschaert that it is time to act. and its very absence is proof that we are dealing with an action, because it is present at a very important event - the final phase of the trialogue on the return directive, which i hear is going well and may be concluded successfully today. this is an important aspect of the fight against illegal migration, the return directive. and if it is adopted at first reading, which is the wish of the slovenian presidency and which we believe is also the ambition of the european parliament, then we will have a new lever to deal more effectively with the phenomenon of illegal migration. the issue of solidarity, of course, has a great political charge in a problem such as this one of illegal migration. but it should be borne in mind that certain elements of solidarity are already there: we had the schengen resource 'schengen facility' for new member states, we have frontex, the commissioner has listed important capacities that member states have contributed to the agency in the name of solidarity, and on a voluntary basis. so i cannot agree that there is no solidarity in the european union. there is, of course, room for improvement in solidarity, but this must be taken into account - and i think mr fava has pointed this out amongst others - as external border control is a competence of the member states. why would you do that? because most people want to. it's very simple. so solidarity has its limits, and the limits are the desire of the member states, most of them, to have competence in the control of the external borders. also, as mrs saks has mentioned, member states do not want immigrant quotas imposed on them from the outside or from above, but they want to decide these things themselves. so these are the frameworks within which we are moving, these are the frameworks within which the slovenian presidency is looking for possibilities for progress, and i think we have already succeeded in achieving a certain number of measures, and we are still working on certain others. perhaps i should also say something about reception centres, as mr moreno sánchez has said: the debate on this is still ongoing and very difficult; it is a very politically sensitive issue, it is not a simple subject, and it is likely that the council will be dealing with it for some time to come. mr özdemir mentioned the issue of asylum: there are statistics on asylum, the asylum system at eu level is working, but we are of course trying to make it work better. the first step was taken with the publication of the green paper on the future of asylum presented by the european commission and the council conclusions adopted at the last justice and home affairs council on improving practical cooperation. i'll end here, i could go on about this very interesting and topical topic. i can assure you, ladies and gentlemen, that your views have been taken into account and will be taken into account in the further course of this debate, and that the slovenian presidency is counting on your cooperation in making progress on this dossier.
the commission's vice-president - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all, i would like to return to the heart of this debate, which is frontex, and i would like to make a few clarifications. mr fava, in particular, insisted on knowing whether the equipment used by frontex was fully operational. it is true that frontex depends on the member states for the technical equipment necessary for the operations coordinated by the agency and, so far, the agency is satisfied with the way in which the member states actually provide the technical equipment they have made available to it in the crate database. so obviously a next step would be to actually put in place a more binding system for member states, through an amendment to the agency's basic regulation. the commission refers to this in its evaluation report and discussions with frontex and the member states will be continued to this end. frontex has concluded technical agreements with the majority of member states on the conditions for using its equipment. it is obviously beyond the means of frontex to buy very expensive equipment. but the commission recommended in its evaluation report that frontex should buy or lease the equipment that is used frequently: night vision goggles, small radar equipment, heat detection devices, etc. i also want to say, since mr moreno sánchez raised these points in particular, that there are geographical areas which are particularly exposed. we could say that we could imagine permanent operations centres here. frontex is working on it. so there are many other questions and i apologize for not listing all the speakers, but i have made specific notes. many of you have raised the question of whether frontex as such can come to the rescue of shipwrecked people. it should be remembered, however, that the responsibility for the care and rescue of shipwrecked persons lies with the member states. frontex has no mandate in this area. that being said, i think it is safe to say that in the operations coordinated by frontex many lives have fortunately been saved and more and more should be saved, because what we have been told here and there by all these absolute tragedies represented by these shipwrecked people, poor people who have often been exploited, is obviously a major concern in these operations. i would like to repeat briefly what the president and the minister have just said, and to recall that, as mr gaubert has said, the main point in all this is that europe should start to manage migration flows. and to manage migration flows, we will not actually do it only through frontex, through external border surveillance. it is clear that we need a legal framework which will gradually enable europe to have a response which is a european response to all these migration problems. and i have to say that one of the big tasks that awaits me is to write a new communication on this comprehensive approach to migration, which must indeed take into account all the aspects that you have raised. i would add that a successful migration policy cannot be achieved without close cooperation with the countries of origin of these immigrants. and what has been said on this subject is that all efforts are welcome to strengthen this cooperation with the immigration countries. as you have just pointed out, mr minister, the trilogue on the text of the return seems to be progressing. it is also one of the cornerstones of this overall immigration policy. of course, this policy must be global, it must also be based on solidarity. there has to be solidarity. we have talked a lot tonight about the rescue at sea, but there are also the eastern frontiers of europe. of course, and i will end on this, the treatment of illegal immigrants must be done in accordance with the fundamental rights to which europe has attached its vocation. so all this requires a truly comprehensive approach, one which is both humane and at the same time extremely serious and rigorous if we want europe not to be a fortress, but open, but open under rules which seem reasonable to us, respectful of people and, at the same time, also attentive to the success of integration efforts in the various member states. because there can be no successful immigration policy without integration. i simply wanted to say that, apologizing to the members for not answering all the questions asked, knowing that i will be listening to parliament to try to lay the foundations for this comprehensive immigration policy.
in writing. the external borders of the european union, whether they are land or sea, protect all member states from possible threats from illegal migration, trafficking and organised crime. the tools proposed by the european commission in the development of frontex, namely the high-performance border surveillance systems, technical equipment and rapid intervention teams are certainly welcome. but the effort to strengthen the borders must be a joint, european effort and not a singular one of the states on the border. in addition, measures need to be taken not only at the union's border but also at the borders of the states neighbouring the union. recall that political stability, the development of democracy, the economy and the raising of living standards in the third countries neighbouring the union will considerably reduce the pressure on the borders; therefore, cooperation with the competent authorities of these countries is a major priority. the projects advanced by the commission urgently need adequate funding so that they can be put into practice in the nearest future.
the meeting of the parties to the convention on biological diversity in bonn will also discuss the issue of forest biodiversity. this is a sensitive subject for which no lasting solution has yet been found. forest biodiversity is threatened by illegal logging that is taking place around the globe. they result in substantial and largely irreversible reductions in biodiversity. in addition, deforestation is the third largest contributor to global warming. pech expressed its position on the significant climate impact of deforestation, the long-term economic benefits and the importance of keeping forests intact in its november 2007 resolution on trade and climate change. i also welcome the eu's initiative through the action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade. i have mentioned actions at european level which, unfortunately, are not producing the desired results. for example, in implementing the action plan, 70% of eu countries failed to take any concrete action by april 2007. we need to find a global solution as quickly as possible. i encourage the eu delegations at the bonn conference to support the drafting of a standard definition of what constitutes illegal logging and to support the rational exploitation of forests. in addition, i encourage the launch of discussions on the launch of a global mechanism to pursue the legality of logging and trade in timber.
madam president, i wish to stress that the reform of the wto has to be embedded into a reshaping of the whole institutional set-up which deals with the governance of global challenges. just look at the effects of global warming and the financial crisis of huge economic imbalances. open trade has to be fair. in addition it has to be linked with policies that help poor countries to develop, through agriculture in particular. the formidable rises in food prices are going to fuel protectionism and restrictions unless we focus on developing food production throughout the world. the rises in the prices of basic commodities has compounded a very complicated general state of affairs. food will increasingly be seen as a national security problem both in wealthy and poor countries. therefore the reform of the cap, the eu development aid policy and the energy policies have to be examined by considering the dramatic changes in the international context.

in writing. as a member of the european parliament's delegation for relations with the gulf states, i would like to stress the importance of the signing of the free trade agreement between the european union and the gulf cooperation council in the near future. the conclusion of the agreement in 2008 would be a key prerequisite for the intensification of economic relations between the two regions, and the need to ensure the energy security of the european union reflects the high level of importance and urgency of this issue. given the focus of current trade on energy, it is essential that the future agreement addresses cooperation in this area and its strengthening in a clear and comprehensive manner. this would multiply and facilitate the implementation of joint energy projects, including with eu member states in the black sea region, which would benefit from new opportunities for development and cooperation. it is therefore a priority to establish a well-defined timetable for the completion of the current negotiations, as well as articulating the major goal of mutual benefits, which would lead not only to deepening economic relations between the eu and the gulf states, but also to strengthening stability and sustained development in general.
mr president, i would like to stress that tackling climate change requires more extensive actions than those focusing on transport and energy. avoiding deforestation should also be at the core of the eu climate change mitigation strategy, as a highly cost-effective way of reducing greenhouse gas emissions fairly quickly. avoiding deforestation can be achieved only by a mix of regulatory approach and market-based instruments. civil society has repeatedly exposed the way the eu actively contributes to global deforestation by allowing illegal timber to freely enter its market. it is vital that the eu introduces legislation to ensure that only timber and timber products from legal sources are placed on the eu market. this regulatory approach should be complemented by a set of market-based instruments specifically designed for forestry, such as charges for premature harvesting of forests or incentives for sustainable forest management. however, in order to use market-based instruments more widely in forestry, we need to clarify which instruments work best, to what extent they can be used and how they can be correlated with regulatory law. i call on the commission to present an analysis of the most appropriate market-based instruments for the forestry sector, and to outline the suitable context for these instruments to be used and combined with other policy tools.
it should be stressed that the european union will only be able to achieve its emission reduction targets through the cooperation and strong commitment of local communities. the market instruments used for environmental and other related policy purposes must be known to them. the commission has taken initiatives such as the exchange of emission certificates, the fuel quality directive, the euro standards for vehicles, the directive on the procurement of clean and energy-efficient road vehicles, and the euro 6 standard for vehicles. in october, the commission will come up with a proposal for a revision of the eurovignette directive, based on the internalisation of external costs, including those related to the environment. as rapporteur for the tran committee opinion on the proposal for a directive on clean and energy-efficient vehicles, i think it is important to calculate the cost of a vehicle over its entire life cycle, taking into account not only the initial purchase price but also the price of the fuel used, carbon dioxide emissions, etc. i hope that as many local authorities as possible will participate effectively in these consultations.

in writing. the emergence of economic and monetary union (emu) led not only to the creation of a simple free trade area at union level, but also gave the union greater political power at international level, set the criteria for the reunification of the continent and the creation of the single currency, the euro, which was able to rival the us dollar. the advantage of emu is that it has ensured low inflation and interest rates for the benefit of consumers and businesses and has encouraged the soundness and sustainability of public finances, and the introduction of the single currency has led to the disappearance of the costs of foreign exchange, facilitated trade and price equivalence in the countries that now constitute the euro area. now, europe is preparing to mark a decade since the single currency was adopted, and even though the southern eu countries are facing a number of difficulties as a result of the single currency, the authorities have not yet complained. analysts explain that despite the changes in the financial markets in the united states, europe has remained stable. i would also say that the success of the euro can also be recognised by the fact that the danes, who initially refused to introduce the single currency, now want the euro. the introduction of the euro remains an important objective for romania at present, with further significant efforts needed to meet the convergence criteria and to increase the competitiveness of romanian firms within the single market.
in writing. 2008 marks the 10th anniversary of the creation of the european central bank (ecb), one of the most daring projects of european construction. ten years on, the results of economic and monetary union are undeniable successes. the exclusive use of economic criteria in the ecb's decision-making and the removal of any political influence in the decision-making process have made this project a success, which has benefited the economies of the participating member states. at the time of romania's accession to the eu, both the government and the central bank assessed the prospect of romania joining emu in 2014. the adoption of the euro in romania implies prior participation in the exchange rate mechanism (erm ii) for a period of two years, i.e. from 2012. for these time horizons to remain feasible, efforts to coordinate the government's fiscal policies with those of the central bank must be continued, and restraint and prudence in budget execution are needed. in order to keep inflation within the parameters proposed by the nbr, the temptations specific to election years must be avoided. the bnr's inflation targeting policy must be supported by fiscal stability, responsible decisions in the romanian parliament and balanced and efficient budget execution at the level of all state institutions.

in writing. the continuing and rapid depletion of deep-sea fish stocks and insufficient measures to protect deep-sea biodiversity require urgent action to ensure the conservation and sustainable use of fish species. although the 2002 and 2004 recommendations of the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) point out that most species are below safe biological limits, the european union has reduced its fishing effort too little to ensure sustainable fishing. the commission communication on the review of deep-sea fish stocks confirms that the current levels of exploitation of deep-sea stocks need to be reduced and that the measures in force have not been sufficiently implemented to be effective. therefore, before adopting new management measures, it is necessary to determine the reasons for the non-application of existing measures and the reasons for the failure of member states to fulfil their commitments or for their delay in fulfilling them. furthermore, the eu must make considerable efforts to fully and effectively implement un general assembly resolution 61/105 on deep-sea fishing zones and the protection of vulnerable marine ecosystems.
in writing. consulting and involving as many stakeholders as possible in the development, implementation and monitoring of the application of european legislation is an objective necessity for the smooth running of the legislative process, for correcting errors and for avoiding biased opinions. open dialogue with representatives of all actors involved in this process is the basis of our democratic system and an important source of information, provided it is conducted in full transparency. for this reason, the initiative to introduce a legislative , even voluntary, footprint for both commission documents and reports in the european parliament is welcome. consulting as many stakeholders as possible, including adversaries, and making the process itself transparent are essential for the development of complex and honest legislation covering all aspects of the field, ensuring that all points of view are effectively balanced and harmonised, conflicts of interest are avoided and subsequent shortcomings are prevented. the correct exchange of information on lobbying organisations operating alongside the european institutions will in the long term not only facilitate the legislative process but also ensure transparent and fair cooperation between the commission, parliament and the council, the ultimate beneficiary of which is undoubtedly the european citizen.

on the other hand, we also have to secure fair trade rules for access by our industry to raw materials. it is a fact that the european union is a net importer of raw materials and that it will remain so. we are now facing stronger competition on our supply markets, as well as rising prices owing to heightened competition from a number of emerging economies. at the same time, those emerging economies are raising barriers to access to their raw materials, thereby distorting competition. fair access to raw materials under transparent conditions is therefore an essential part of the equation in our global competitiveness strategy. the commission’s intention in the years to come is to use all the available instruments to maintain a sustainable supply of raw materials for our industries. in doing so, it will pursue a comprehensive and balanced strategy. as parliament rightly emphasises, that strategy must take into account not only the interests of our industries and our competitiveness, but also the interests of the poorer countries. as regards the development angle, we must, and will, make a distinction between, on the one hand, justified measures maintained by poorer developing countries, such as export taxes, which are indispensable for those countries’ budgets and, on the other hand, measures imposed by emerging economies as part of their industrial policy and which distort competition on world markets. i appreciate mr assis’ comment on r&d commitments, which also need to be increased in this connection. i would like to thank parliament for supporting us on this policy. we will keep you informed on the further implementation of our strategy.

the chairman of the council. - ladies and gentlemen, the rapporteur is mrs ţicău, mr grosch, the honourable members and the other members. in july 2007, the european commission published draft legislative acts, namely a proposal for a regulation on the conditions for the exercise of the activity of road haulage operator, a proposal for a regulation on access to the international road transport market and a proposal for a regulation on access to the international bus transport market. the portuguese presidency started work on the regulation on access to the international freight market, while the slovenian presidency continued its work and opened the remaining two files. parallel to the work of the working group, we also started informal discussions with the rapporteurs in the european parliament. at the april tte council, we ministers held a political debate on a package of key issues, which produced the following conclusions. first, cabotage is a key open issue in the context of the regulation on access to the freight transport market. the majority of member states supported in principle a compromise solution allowing three cabotage operations within seven days of unloading in the host member state. however, several delegations, supported also by the commission, requested that transit cabotage be made available in addition to the empty carriage. the presidency is now working towards a compromise solution within the council. secondly, in connection with the regulation on access to the professions, a compromise must be found with regard to the national electronic register and the transport operator. in fact, we are very, very close to agreeing on a timetable for the establishment of this registry. thirdly, as regards the regulation on international bus transport, it is necessary to continue the discussion at working group level. we have agreed that the solutions of the other two regulations will be applied in a meaningful way in this one. the slovenian presidency intends to reach political agreement on all three proposals for regulations at the tte council on 13 june 2008. i would like to emphasise that we will try to take your amendments into account as far as possible and thus try to bring our positions as close as possible. the slovenian presidency is committed to contributing to the consolidation and completion of the single market. i believe that the rapidly expanding road transport sector is one of the cornerstones of the single market and the free movement of goods and people and that the modernisation of community legislation is essential to improve efficiency, better visibility and ensure fair competition. the slovenian presidency fully supports the objectives pursued by the proposals for all three regulations. i would like to stress that the slovenian presidency is aware of the existing restrictions on the european union's transport market and is therefore committed not only to strengthening the rules and control mechanisms for cabotage but also to enforcing uniform provisions on access to the profession. electronic registers in particular can increase the efficiency and transparency of our business and significantly reduce the administrative burden. in conclusion, i would like to thank the members of the european parliament, in particular the rapporteurs, mr grosch and mrs ţicău, for the excellent exchange of views. i would like to reiterate that the slovenian presidency will do everything in our power to strike a balance between the various interests and at the same time ensure that the solutions we adopt will enable the european road transport industry to improve its efficiency and become more competitive. i am here to express my hope and wish that the constructive dialogue will continue and that agreement with the european parliament will be reached as soon as possible.
member of the commission. − the regulations on access to the international road passenger transport market and to the road freight market, respectively, together with the regulation on access to the occupation of road operator form a package. these subjects are inextricably linked. i am very pleased to see these three texts put to the vote today to establish your position at first reading. i would like to thank your rapporteurs, mrs ticău and mr grosch, and all the members who have contributed to the work. a rapid agreement is necessary for the following reasons: the european council of march 2007 expressed its wish to do so; the sector concerned, more than 900 000 enterprises, wants the conditions for access to the profession to be harmonised in order to benefit from fair competition and clear rules on this narrow but thorny problem of cabotage. fifteen years after the first regulations on access to road transport, the market remains fragmented, with 27 national variants of rules governing access to the profession and the definition of the honour required for access. not to mention, once again, the divergent interpretations of the notion of 'temporary' in relation to cabotage. it was therefore also time to boost progress on the integration of the internal market in road transport. a quick settlement is possible. i have a feeling that your position and that of the council can be even more in line with one another. with the help of the slovenian and french presidencies, i believe that an agreement can be reached soon. i can assure you, at this stage, of my support, at least in principle, for a large part of the amendments proposed by the committee on transport and tourism. since the commission's detailed position on each of the amendments tabled has already been forwarded to the responsible services of parliament, my reservations or comments will concentrate on only a few points. first, the cabotage issue seems to be a major point of this package. but no solution will be good unless it is controllable. the essential quality of the commission's proposal is precisely the clarity, simplicity and controllability of the mechanism introduced: three operations within seven days of an international shipment. this link with international transport is generally recognised and, precisely for this reason, i understand the interest of amendment no 17 to the grosch report, which provides for cabotage operations to be carried out in a transit country on the shortest return route. but the wording of the amendment makes it difficult to control - that is why i cannot support it. however, in order to avoid empty runs, it seems to me that a provision can be made which provides that one of the three operations within a seven-day period may be carried out in a transit country within a maximum of three days. i would have no difficulty in supporting an amendment to that effect. as in amendments nos 18, 37, 40, 44 and 47, which provide that restrictions on the number and duration of cabotage operations will be phased out, with the aim of being phased out in 2014. we have to take account of the market reality in the different member states. tax, social, wage conditions are still very disparate because of the lack of sufficient harmonisation, and i fear that they will remain the same in 2014. the proposed package will certainly contribute to this harmonisation in terms of control of access to the profession, but it could not guarantee a sufficient degree of harmonisation on its own. in those circumstances, an automatic liberalisation of cabotage would have the effect of distorting, rather than strengthening, conditions of competition. a clause for a later review of this matter seems to me therefore more appropriate. it is to be noted that, pending that review, it is self-evident that the regulation in no way prevents member states from fully opening their cabotage markets provided that they do so without discrimination against all other member states or on the basis of agreements between national governments which predate the community rules in force on market access. amendment no 21, as drafted, omits these clarifications and therefore cannot be supported by the commission. as regards access to the profession, the aspect of honour and serious breaches of the law is paramount. the procedure you propose, regarding the withdrawal of the honourable in case of serious violation of the law, seems to me to have a great deterrent, but remains appropriate. i particularly welcome amendment no 104 in mrs ticău's report, which sets out a very clear list of these violations. we can therefore support parliament's proposal on article 6. the european business register is of particular importance for ensuring good repute. and here, in principle, we support amendments nos 70, 72 to 78 and 114, which provide for the rapid and progressive introduction of interconnected national registers. finally, the draft regulation allows micro-enterprises to use so-called external managers. in other words, managers who do not work directly in these micro-enterprises. the 27th amendment sets no limits on this possibility which, in my opinion, should remain the exception rather than the rule. therefore, i cannot support him. i could instead support amendment 109, which provides for a reasonable limit of 50 vehicles. finally, as regards the question of the 12 days, i would like to refer to the former amendment no 102 in mrs ticău's report, which seeks to reinstate the so-called 12 days for coaches. i agree with the choice of the house to vote on this amendment in the context of mr grosch's report on buses. the commission has not yet decided on the content. the social partners are currently working on this issue and we must wait for the outcome of their first exchanges in order not to legislate in haste. a more detailed review of the issue will be required as soon as an agreement is found between these partners, without however slowing down the progress of an agreement on cabotage and the register.
the reporter. - i would like to begin by thanking the commission, the council, the co-rapporteurs, in particular mr grosch, mr sterckx, mrs lichtenberger and all the colleagues with whom i collaborated on this report. the proposal for a regulation on access to the occupation of road haulage operator is important because it addresses the 4.5 million road transport workers and over 900 000 european enterprises. we have tried to have as wide a consultation as possible with those who are active in this field and, to this end, the tran committee held a public debate last october to gather as many views as possible on the proposal for a regulation. the regulation replaces directive 96/26, which was implemented differently by the member states. the proposal for a regulation lays down the common criteria according to which an undertaking has access to the occupation of road haulage operator, a fixed establishment, the operation of an operational centre, access to a sufficient number of parking spaces, the criteria for proving financial capacity, good repute, the role of the transport manager and the conditions which he must fulfil, and i am referring here to the certificate of professional competence and good repute, and the obligation for member states to set up national electronic registers which will be interconnected. the tran committee has tabled 193 amendments to the commission proposal. the parliament, the tran committee, therefore opted for a text which dealt only with serious and very serious offences, the latter being defined in a new annex to the regulation, and for serious offences the commission to come up with a list of offences the repetitive nature of which may result in the loss of a road transport licence. that list will be approved by the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. as regards the national electronic registers to be interconnected by 1 january 2012, they will be based on a common minimum structure to be presented by the commission by 1 january 2010. the electronic registers shall have a public and a confidential section. the public section will contain data on road transport operators and road transport managers and the confidential section will contain data on offences committed or sanctions imposed and will be accessible only by the competent authorities, subject to the provisions on the protection of personal data. i would point out that this confidential data may be kept in separate registers. as regards the issue of a certificate of professional competence, the tran committee opted for the abolition of a fixed number of hours of training, preferring the obligation to take a written examination followed, at the discretion of each member state, by an oral examination. another proposed amendment is that a transport manager be sanctioned only for those acts which are attributable to him. thus, any decision to impose a sanction may be challenged and the recording of sanctions in the electronic register will only take place after a final decision to this effect. the tran committee considered that it was sufficient for a company to be able to prove its financial capacity on the basis of annual accounts verified by a notary or a duly accredited person, on the basis of a bank guarantee or other financial instrument, such as insurance. the 80% threshold for immediate liquidity was therefore abandoned in favour of a minimum threshold for capital and reserves. the tran committee also considers it important that the euro value be set annually, rather than every 5 years as was envisaged in the commission proposal. i also proposed that article 22 of the commission proposal, which set out certain priority rights differentially for the different member states, be deleted and amendment no 52 was introduced, which allows persons who can prove that they have continuously managed the road transport activity for the last 10 years before the regulation came into force to be exempted from examination. i've proposed that the number of vehicles managed by an outside manager be limited to 50, and the number of companies to 4. as regards the internal transport manager, the socialist group proposes limiting the number of vehicles directly managed by a transport manager to 250. we consider this necessary because the transport manager must also have decent working conditions. the commission has also tabled two amendments to the tran committee concerning the 12-day derogation for the rest period of bus drivers engaged in international passenger transport. an agreement is expected between employers and unions and therefore the two amendments will be reintroduced in mr grosch's report.
i would like to congratulate the two rapporteurs on their work and refer to the report by mr ticău. i welcome the introduction of qualitative access criteria to the road transport operator profession in order to improve the quality of licensed operators and not restrict their access to the profession. whether we are talking about people or material goods, the road transport operator profession involves carrying out activities that are indispensable for the economic development of the union in full accordance with the lisbon objectives of boosting economic activity in the european area. i believe that the implementation of this regulation will lead to an increase in the number of jobs, but also to a greater degree of safety and fairness in road transport throughout the european union. once again, congratulations to the reporters.

member of the commission. - i am pleased to see the consensus emerging on the essential aspects of the road package. i'm referring specifically to the registry and the withdrawal of certain abilities in the case of serious violations of the law. but it's clear that the cabotage issue is more problematic. but i would remind you that the notion of temporary cabotage, which is now in force, leaves serious legal uncertainties. this is not acceptable for the sector in question. no rule is perfect, but the one proposed by the commission - three operations within one week of an international shipment - is at least clear and much easier to control. it does not introduce more or less cabotage into the member states taken separately, but a better-performed cabotage which is, on the one hand, controllable and, on the other, logistically efficient. for those who want more cabotage, i say that the internal market is being built up gradually and must go hand in hand with harmonization. and since harmonization has been mentioned, i would remind you that certain matters relating to tax, wage and social harmonization are either within the competence of the member states or can be achieved by unanimity. in this context, we can say that a full opening without guarantees and safeguards, with cabotage being by definition temporary, would send us back to the legal uncertainty of today. the european commission therefore accepts that the liberalisation of cabotage is a long-term objective. on the other hand, we will have to monitor developments closely and, in this context, we are prepared to report in 2012. finally, i note the concerns expressed on numerous occasions on the question of the 12 days for tourist trips. if the european parliament is in favour of postponing the vote on the regulation on international passenger transport, the european commission will not oppose it because, indeed, an agreement on the register and cabotage is needed in the nearest possible future, but at the same time, the widest possible consensus is needed between the social partners on the question of the 12 days.

mr president, i want to address a matter of principle, namely the neo-conservative tendencies of this house on the eu foreign and security policy. seemingly some of us believe that the substance of any foreign policy is dependent on the nature of the political regime pursuing it; therefore it looks as though our main objective has become the export of our political model. unfortunately, the european union has neither the decision-making mechanisms nor the means to promote effectively an interventionist policy. we must change this approach, adopting realism as a base of our external action. this means: clearly defining the scope of our foreign policy in accordance with the common existential interests of european citizens; balancing the scope with the resources, while acknowledging that this world contains actors that are different from us and do not always necessarily share our values; learning to operate with them, and giving up narcissism to look for negotiations and cooperation with our opponents, and not only with our friends. certainly we should try to make as many as possible of our foreign interlocutors into our friends, but before doing that and while doing that i believe we have to learn to operate with those who are not like us. i believe that we could be more appealing through our means, through our behaviour in promoting our goals rather than by our targets, thus eventually promoting our model in the world.
mr president, the world in which the eu is called upon to further its integration towards a truly common foreign policy gets more complex every day. the prospect of economic recession, fuelled by the current financial crisis and increasing energy costs, the unsatisfactory status of transatlantic relations and the increasing assertiveness of russia, which confront europe more and more with old-style geopolitical challenges for which it is no longer equipped, are only a reflection of the current international environment. in this context, against the background of increasing eu dependence on russian supplies, energy tends to become the litmus test for success or failure in achieving the aim of a common eu foreign policy, because it makes all the difference whether europe agrees to create a single energy market and consequently approaches suppliers, primarily russia, with one voice, or continues to preserve the current national divides and give priority to bilateral preferential supply contracts destined to satisfy its increasing energy needs. today world politics is first and foremost about gas and oil.
today marks the 88th anniversary of the trianon peace treaty, signed by the great powers of europe at the end of the first world war, which set out security policy decisions that ignored or merely guaranteed the rights of national minorities. the paris peace treaty, signed after world war ii, did not solve the problems. the question of security policy was reduced to guaranteeing the inviolability of borders. most of the borders that existed then have disappeared, and czechoslovakia and yugoslavia no longer exist. the minority issue remains. we hungarians have been to 8 countries, of which so far only slovenia has been able to resolve the rights of the hungarian community in a reassuring way. the report says that progress is needed to ensure effective protection of minority rights in line with european standards. but by what european standards? it would be good to promote within the eu what we expect from the western balkans. as the latin proverb says, "if you want peace, prepare for war". today we want a safe europe. the rights of national minorities must be regulated within and outside the eu by means of the territorial and cultural autonomy that has been established in the western half of europe. thank you, sir.

vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament has been a great help to us in the last few years. i would like to answer two questions briefly. firstly, cooperation on security issues, which has been very strongly presented by frau in 't veld, and which is about how we find the right balance between the security needs of our american friends and the demands we ourselves make on individual freedom and the individual rights of our citizens. i would like to make it quite clear to you, madam president: the commission fully shares your concerns and i will of course convey to the honourable member the criticism you have expressed about the lack of transparency in the procedure and ask him to ensure greater transparency. we are talking to the americans before we can engage in anything about the principles that should guide us in working together on such matters. if there is no agreement on these principles, there can hardly be agreement on individual issues. this is of course a topic for the meeting in ljubljana next week. i do not want to say anything more about poultry, but it has been raised by several people here. it's always good to know what you're talking about. so it's also important to know that this is not a food safety issue that we're talking about here. for many years the european food safety authority has declared that american poultry imports do not pose the slightest risk to the health of consumers. we are not talking about a veterinary problem, we are talking about a purely commercial issue which must be dealt with from the point of view of what our interests are and how best to defend them. i think i have said all that is necessary, and there are no differences of opinion in the commission. the commission has from the outset declared itself ready not to let this - i must say - somewhat bizarre conflict become a burden and to put an end to the problem.
in writing. as vice-president of the envi commission, i encourage the eu representatives present at the meeting with the us officials to consider solutions to the climate change issue. climate change is a global challenge to which we must prepare a global response. europe is working on this. we expect the same example from our neighbours overseas. i'm glad that the united states will join the efforts of the international community after 2012, after the kyoto protocol expires. i also appreciate that the president of the united states finally acknowledged that we need legislation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. i encourage the eu representatives to discuss a real percentage cut to really help stop global warming. we can't just accept that we need legislation and then when we get to the numbers, we back off. at the same time, future discussions on the collaborative climate change framework must be based on real studies on renewable energy sources. i am mainly talking about first-generation biofuels. it is necessary to maintain a low rate of use and a low level of subsidies. this will protect biodiversity and avoid food price increases due to the reduction of agricultural land.

in writing. since its creation, the gsp has been one of the main instruments of the eu's trade and development policies. the main objective of eu development policy and the gsp is to contribute to poverty eradication, the promotion of sustainable development and good governance, principles recognised by international conventions and instruments such as the millennium declaration, the rio declaration 1992, the ilo declaration 1998. through the implementation of the gsp since 1971, the eu has facilitated international trade with developing and least developed countries, providing them with the technical assistance necessary to comply with international conventions and the appropriate institutional and regulatory capacity to take advantage of international trade and the gsp. at the same time, upon verified notification and after informing the ep, the ec may apply the sanction of temporary withdrawal of preferences to countries that violate the criteria for inclusion in the list of beneficiaries. the report stresses the importance of the public consultation process, the involvement of the targeted beneficiaries and the strengthening of the ep's democratic control. as both the gsp and the list of beneficiary countries are reviewed every 3 years, the council is requested not to delay their submission in time for approval by the ep, avoiding syncopation in international trade. i congratulate the reporter.
in writing. according to the pittella report, the sector inquiry looked at the competitive situation in payment systems, including card schemes, credit bureaus, inter-bank cooperation, pricing and banking policies. the investigation shows that there are significant differences between the fees paid for bank cards. it was found that most national debit card networks charge significantly lower interchange fees than international networks and that in most member states most banks make the granting of mortgages, personal loans and loans to smes conditional on the opening of a current account. in general, the consumer does not have the same bargaining power when entering into a contractual relationship with the bank of which he becomes a customer. the customer signs a contract, which he doesn't always read, and even if he does and wants to propose changes, it's not possible. in this context, i believe that the responsible regulators should ensure that the form of contracts offered by banking institutions also protects the interest of the consumer and not only that of the banks. i consider it mandatory that a customer opening an account receives in advance a summary statement of all applicable costs for the entire period of use of the account.
in writing. the main points of the proposed regulation are the introduction of the precautionary principle and the issuing of a fishing licence subject to an assessment that these activities do not have harmful effects on marine ecosystems. as the fictitious rapporteur, i considered it necessary that these assessments should be based on criteria harmonised at community level, which would be reviewed by the commission to ensure a uniform assessment by all states. i also proposed the establishment of an electronic mapping system to create a database of vulnerable marine ecosystems, which would reduce the costs and effort of carrying out a fishing licence assessment. in other words, the proposed elements were introduced to improve the efficiency of the system and to ensure optimal protection of marine biodiversity. it is also essential that by the end of 2008 the commission establishes a list of areas to be closed, indicating both confirmed sites and those where vulnerable marine ecosystems are likely to be present. however, the role that member states must play in protecting marine life must not be overlooked by implementing the obligations of the habitats directive and the designation of marine ecosystems under national jurisdiction in the natura 2000 network.
madam president, trafficking may be an illegal market, but is nonetheless a market, having both a supply and a demand side. a country where there is significant demand plays an equally active part in trafficking as an origin country. besides being a leftover of slavery in our times, trafficking constitutes continued defiance and infringement of the law and is linked to other criminal practices, such as money laundering, violence, smuggling, prostitution, tax evasion, fraud and forced labour. trafficking produces dangerous reversals within the order of values in our society, preserving old inequalities – women and children are seen as merchandise – and generating new ones. the money that traffickers earn undermines the belief in the value of labour and fair business. it is necessary for all member states urgently to ratify the council of europe convention on trafficking and to apply the measures they have agreed, starting with combating the root cause of trafficking for prostitution, which is male demand for women and girls.

in writing. −the new amended form of the report respects the agreement between the social partners on the reintroduction of the 12-day derogation for rest time for coach drivers engaged in international passenger transport. i voted for amendment no 31, which lays down the conditions for drivers employed in an international transport service to have their weekly rest period extended to 12 consecutive 24-hour periods following a previous weekly rest period. these conditions are: the international occasional service must include at least 24 hours in a member state or third country other than the one in which the service started; the weekly rest period after the application of the derogation must always be at least a normal weekly rest period of 45 hours; a compensatory rest period of 24 hours is taken continuously before the end of the third week following the application of the derogation; if the driving period is continuous between 22.00 and 06.00, the vehicle is equipped with two drivers or the driving period is reduced to three hours; from 1 january 2014, the application of this derogation is only possible for vehicles equipped with recording equipment in accordance with european provisions.

in writing. the forest fires in greece, italy and spain in the summer of 2007, the floods in romania and the uk, led to an increase in calls to improve the effectiveness of the eu's disaster response capacity. the frequency of climate change-related disasters is increasing and requires multilateral and coordinated responses that mobilise all available resources, taking into account issues such as speed, effectiveness and financial return. the commission's proposed measures to help boost the eu's response to disasters include strengthening the monitoring and information centre (mic), improving the response capacity of european civil protection and better coordination between the un and the red cross on humanitarian aid delivery. it also calls for the creation of a european training network on disaster response, the establishment of early warning systems and the use of the european emergency number 112, which is not well known in all member states. in romania, only 30% of citizens know that this number can be called in an emergency from any eu country and national authorities need to continue their efforts towards promoting this number to react quickly to climate change problems and beyond.
commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, what the commission is reminding us of, we know all too well: there are a huge number of europeans living in poverty, including extreme poverty. those who don't know should take a big part of the blame that a rich society based on the principles of justice and solidarity like ours works so that the state of the poor europeans would have more seats in this parliament than germany. poverty is not an abstraction, it is a way of life that particularly affects women and children. women, including those in employment, face increased risks due to the structural wage gap, their concentration in low-paid, poorly unionized sectors and in the informal economy, given their prevalence among single-parent families. poverty is inherited. economic poverty of parents favours cultural poverty of children, through reduced access to education, political poverty, through low participation or exclusion from decision-making, social poverty, through reduced involvement in civic activities and isolation. it creates inequalities that are deeper than those derived from different purchasing power. a little coherence between statements and actions requires more than raising awareness. political decisions are needed to correct the situation. in the union we cannot speak of a lack of resources but of an often unfair distribution of them, of rules that perpetuate exclusion. it's a shared responsibility, including for companies that, for their own sake, need to move beyond the point where funding a foundation to protect stray dogs in the neighborhood was the only form of social responsibility.
mr president, eradicating poverty and social exclusion is one of the major objectives of the european union. the year 2010 must therefore be decisive in implementing the european strategy in this area. of the 78 million citizens living at risk of poverty, 19 million are children. unfortunately, there are still no european programmes and funds that are aimed at improving the situation of children. it is true that the european union provides funds for fruit and milk in schools or money for school education, but i believe that a coherent strategy and concrete programmes targeting children from poor families are needed. at the same time, we must also focus on the other disadvantaged groups, especially young people, for whom policies must be set up and substantial amounts of structural funds allocated. it is also important to stress that we cannot create the conditions for sustainable social development without the necessary financial resources. i believe that the €17 million allocated is insufficient in relation to the needs for social inclusion and poverty reduction that europe has today. last but not least, the fight against poverty and social exclusion must be linked to existing programmes. both the european social fund and the european progres programme should be used to finance the priorities of the european year against poverty.
in writing. thank you to the rapporteur for his cooperation in drafting this report. in europe, one person in six lives below the poverty line, a figure that does not include statistics from romania and bulgaria. although in most member states the gap between women and men in poverty is increasingly narrowing and the average gap is 2% in poverty and persistent poverty, i would like to draw attention to the reality in the new member states. in romania and bulgaria, the number of women at risk of poverty is over ten percent higher than that of men. women are also much more exposed to social exclusion. it should not be overlooked that the ideas of solidarity, social justice and poverty eradication are challenges not only within the european union but also its involvement on the world economic and political scene. i therefore welcome the inclusion in the final text of the issue of the difference between men and women in a more general article. i also consider it important to link the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion with the millennium development goals and, in particular, with the international day for the eradication of poverty.
in writing. the constitution of the international labour organization states: poverty, no matter where it is, is a danger to the prosperity of all. i therefore stress the importance of the amendment on preventing and combating poverty by pursuing multidimensional policies at national, regional and local level, ensuring active participation of citizens in society and the labour market. social protection reforms and active inclusion policies have made a decisive contribution to accelerating economic growth and creating more jobs in europe. romania had one of the highest economic growth rates in the eu in the first quarter of 2008, with growth of 8.2% (while the european average is 2.5%, according to eurostat), but, nevertheless, people with low education, lacking skills, especially from rural areas, children, young people, people with disabilities and roma are at significant risk of poverty. i congratulate the rapporteur on her work and believe that the policies developed by the member states, following the european recommendations, should seek to reconcile economic competitiveness and the social well-being of citizens.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank mr harangozó for his report and also for his efforts to achieve a consensual position in his committee on the difficult topic of vulnerable communities and groups. to avoid economic growth being accompanied by social polarisation in our society, cohesion policy targets social exclusion, in particular the integration of vulnerable communities and groups, and it will remain a cohesion policy goal in the future. it is also true that problems identified in the report are at the frontier between territorial cohesion, on the one hand, and social cohesion challenges on the other, and social polarisation and social segregation problems, when concentrated on some territories, become territorial cohesion issues. we face social exclusion in the poorest territories of the european union, but we also have pockets of social deprivation in the richest cities of the european union. the report calls on the commission to present a comprehensive definition of territorial cohesion in the framework of the forthcoming green paper on territorial cohesion, and i can confirm that the green paper to be published at the end of september this year will contribute to the progress towards a common understanding across the union of the concept of territorial cohesion. the report also recognises that the notion of vulnerable groups and communities as such is certainly not an easy one and it should not be limited to the roma communities only. however, it is generally recognised that the situation of roma communities deserves special focus in europe. to address the multi-faceted problems of roma exclusion, we need an integrated approach, and parliament discussed it in depth in january when adopting a resolution on a european strategy on the roma. in the package on the renewed social agenda, the commission will present at the beginning of july its working document on community instruments and policies for roma inclusion. i share the report’s opinion on the need to make greater use of the synergies and complementarities among european policies and also among various financial instruments available. the commission paid much attention to this when negotiating operational programmes of the cohesion policy with the national and regional authorities. as to the issue of making available comparable intra-regional data for all regions in the european union, with special regard to social indicators, while essential, i share the report’s view here: it is a more complex one. as members will be aware, eurostat does not produce data, but manages data provided by the national statistical systems. we have just completed the second edition of the urban audit, covering the period up to 2004 and we clearly see how limited the availability of territorial data is below the nuts 2 classical regional level. to address this challenge and also using the context of preparations of the green paper on territorial cohesion, the directorate general for regional policy worked on improving the quality of research on regional policy, including its statistical bases. as a result, the expenditure 2000-2006 is today broken down to the nuts 3 level, to 20 categories of expenditure at this level, and is available for objective i regions, objective ii, urban, interreg and cohesion fund. rural audit is still a challenge ahead of us. unfortunately, i must admit today that reliable data does not yet exist on where particular excluded groups are concentrated, hence it is impossible to cross-match our newly available information on what and where cohesion policy resources are spent on with the location of such groups. i consider that the margin of progress in this area, as it seems
