on behalf of the ppe-de group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work and for the efforts he has made to reconcile the different points of view. we all agree that vulnerable groups and communities face many difficulties in their development and that they require special attention in the context of cohesion policy and the other financial support instruments available. we have supported at all stages of the work the need to structure the report in two distinct parts: one that targets vulnerable communities, through the prism of ethnicity, and the second, vulnerable communities caused by certain geographical handicaps. unfortunately, however, our request is not reflected in the current form of the report. our group has three amendments for which our vote depends, namely the deletion of recital ee, with the same content as recital i, the clarification of the concept of vulnerable areas by listing them, and the deletion of paragraph 17. i hope we have the rapporteur's approval on this. finally, i would like to emphasise two more ideas: the problems of vulnerable communities from any perspective, be it ethnic and/or geographical, can be tackled more effectively if there is collaboration in this field between local, regional, national and european authorities. at the same time, the role of the education system and public, social and transport infrastructure is indispensable in integrating vulnerable groups and communities. i would like to conclude by saying that our final position is conditional, as i have already said, on the acceptance of the three amendments and, in particular, on the deletion of paragraph 17, which was voted on in the committee. if these amendments are accepted, we will obviously support the report.

limited access to services of general interest make these communities vulnerable groups, which pose an increasing challenge to the cohesion of the european union's territories. this is a relationship (the president of the council is here) - ladies and gentlemen, the original draft of the agency for the cooperation of regulators presented parliament with two options: reject a useless institution or create a more efficient one. the second option was chosen not in spite of the meroni clause but within the limits of the treaty. the amendments, which were generally convergent, adopted in committees and substantially altered the original powers. we therefore expect that the agency's work will strengthen the role of national regulators and support their functioning, enable the technical harmonisation of european networks as a condition for a real internal market and make possible the reciprocal supply of energy between member states, take account of the interests of consumers and closely monitor developments on the energy market. we expect the agency to be a useful instrument of the common energy policy. we do not expect that the granting of these powers will reduce the european commission's responsibilities towards parliament and in the implementation of energy policy, nor that technical decisions will replace political ones. sufficient and affordable energy for all remains our ultimate goal.

in writing. the proposal for a directive debated yesterday and voted on today addresses european immigration policy directly for the first time by setting out standards and procedures for the expulsion of illegal immigrants from the territory of the member states. beyond the objective of legal harmonisation of the situation of migrants, the real challenge of this directive has been to find a compromise that respects human rights and the free movement of persons while taking into account the need for individual security and, above all, collective security. most member states have experienced the phenomenon of immigration, and the measures taken by their governments vary according to the flow of immigrants. i therefore consider that mr weber's report regulates these differences between the immigration policies of the member states, taking account of the principles of each legal system and imposing common standards and enforcement measures. i can therefore say that i voted for this report precisely because of the integrated approach to immigration. measures such as voluntary return to the country of origin, temporary detention and special attention to the protection of unaccompanied minors, as well as access to health and education services, do not constitute a breach of the european convention on human rights, but on the contrary, demonstrate that the european union has taken another step towards creating a common policy on illegal immigration. i also want to congratulate the board and mr. weber on the compromise negotiated.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, i too would like to congratulate you and wish you success in the work you are about to undertake, and i want to tell you that we expect a lot from you. i would like to congratulate mr liberadzki on his report, which is part of the process of simplifying legislation and which virtually brings together and updates the text of four directives into one. previously existing european legislation did not cover the transport of dangerous goods by sea, which was governed by rules established by various multilateral agreements to which member states were parties. it is therefore important that we have community legislation with common rules for all member states for the transport of dangerous goods, for all modes of transport. the existence of these common rules allows dangerous goods to be transferred from one mode of transport to another. in addition to the provisions of this directive, member states may introduce specific requirements for vehicles, wagons and vessels engaged in inland waterway transport into national legislation. the council's proposed amendments introduce two new elements: the first introduces and allows member states to regulate or strictly prohibit the internal transport of dangerous goods within their territory for reasons other than safety. the second amendment requires the commission to provide financial support to member states for the translation into their official languages of european agreements for the transport of dangerous goods by road, rail and sea. however, i believe that all member states should also carry out information campaigns to inform those concerned about the provisions of the new directive. but it's essential to follow these rules. the responsible authorities must ensure that the transport of dangerous goods is carried out only in compliance with the commonly established rules and restrictions.
in writing. – this future directive is a big step forward towards protecting our safety and our environment, as it introduces european rules for transport of dangerous goods not only by road and rail but also by inland waterways. accidents in inland waterways can have an extensive impact and serious consequences such as water poisoning, extinction of wildlife and human health problems. all the more reason to try to reduce the risks by creating common rules for this mode of transport as well. furthermore, i strongly support the inclusion of a provision that member states can regulate or prohibit transport of dangerous goods for reasons other than safety. if we take the case of cyanide, an extremely toxic material, 14% of the cyanide releases into the environment were caused by transport accidents. these figures highlight the vulnerability of cyanide transport and underlines the need for stronger environmental and safety standards. i therefore encourage member states to take the strictest possible measures to regulate transportation of cyanide and, where necessary, to prohibit bulk transportation of cyanide on their territory. sometimes minimising the transport of hazardous goods is just the safest way to minimise the risks.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, every year in the european union some 43 000 people die and another 1.7 million are injured in road accidents. in addition to designing and building safer cars, member states must also invest in road infrastructure safety. road safety impact assessments should demonstrate the road safety implications of the different planning alternatives of an infrastructure project at a strategic level and this should be decisive in the choice of route. the tran committee supported the amendment that allows member states to apply the provisions of this directive, as a set of good practices, also to national road transport infrastructure, not included in the ten-t network, built through the use of all or part of community funds. in order to encourage cycling, especially in urban areas, member states should include in any infrastructure construction option transport roads and special routes for cyclists that intersect as little as possible with major traffic arteries. i consider it essential that member states ensure that appropriate signage is provided to warn road users of road infrastructure sections under repair which may endanger the safety of road users. i also consider that where the implementation of the provisions of this directive gives rise to new obligations for the execution of a road infrastructure project, the commission and the member states should ensure that the amounts allocated are increased accordingly. i would like to conclude by stressing the need for safe parking facilities and i hope that the commissioner will support the amendment i tabled to this effect in the 2009 union budget. i congratulate the reporter.
in writing. this directive is absolutely necessary in particular for major road infrastructure projects. however, it must be borne in mind that important safety issues fall to the member states, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, as a shared responsibility. as designed, and partly built, the trans-european motorway network is among the safest in the world. major problems related to infrastructure safety and traffic safety in general are neither in the ten-t nor, to a large extent, on motorways, problems are on ordinary roads, especially outside cities. for this reason, thorough analysis, competently designed and executed construction projects and effective auditing are needed especially in the regional and local road network, and i therefore believe that member states must take all the sound principles and apply them responsibly not only where they are obliged to do so but also, and especially, where the need is greatest. the rules established by this directive, which are not intended to be binding, particularly from a bureaucratic-administrative point of view, should be adopted as a set of good practices for the continuous improvement of the safety management procedures of all road infrastructure throughout the european union.

in writing. − as rapporteur on black sea cooperation, i would like to express my support for the libicki report simply because the subject it deals with is of a strategic nature, going beyond the baltic sea area and the field of environmental protection. we have discussed a common problem, known to both the baltic and the black sea regions and affecting the whole of europe: energy security and european policy in this area. given the eu's dependence on a limited number of sources, suppliers and transport routes, it is vital that their diversification is the fundamental principle of the european energy security concept. equally important is the development of a coherent european energy policy, based on solidarity and coordination, to avoid the conclusion of bilateral agreements which could harm the interests of other member states and, above all, undermine major projects such as nabucco, which are recognised at european level. i therefore reiterate and insist on the call to the commission and the council to redouble their efforts to ensure the successful implementation of the nabucco project and to articulate a clear common energy policy. the situation in the baltic and the black sea indicates the urgency of taking concrete and firm action.
in writing. - welcomes the position adopted by the european parliament on the construction of a gas pipeline linking russia to germany; the european union needs a common and coherent integrated energy policy and a long-term strategy for ensuring the energy independence of the member states. environmental and geopolitical issues of energy security must be addressed by the european union through a concerted effort of all member states, and not through bilateral treaties concluded by some member states with russia. only in this way can the eu achieve a strong position in the negotiations with russia, avoiding energy resources as a political lever and making the eu an equal partner of russia. in this way we can provide answers to the well-founded frustrations of romanian citizens related to the continuous increase in gas and electricity prices, with important negative socio-economic consequences for romanians and their living standards. at the same time, the solution of a common european energy policy can compensate for the inability of the right-wing governments in bucharest to promote romania's energy interests in relation to russia.
in writing. − stabilising afghanistan is a key security policy challenge for the international community and the fight against terrorism. failure to do so could make western states reluctant to engage in future conflict prevention and resolution interventions and peacekeeping operations. on the other hand, a lasting peace could also benefit afghans who are now experiencing their third decade of conflict and whose state has always been a tool that external actors have used for their own needs. military operations are necessary, but they are not a sufficient condition for the stabilization of afghanistan. an important solution in this process must also be sought at the diplomatic level, and cooperation with iran, india and pakistan is essential, especially in the border areas where insurgent groups are active. in this regard, strengthening democratic structures is of paramount importance and the international community should counter the marginalisation of the afghan government by increasing the importance of the political system and democratic actors at local and regional level. the european union has the image of a humanitarian organisation in afghanistan, but to play a more important role, europeans must take into account that poverty and instability are not solved by weapons and violence, but rather by measures that bring about the well-being of the afghan people. it is with this hope that i voted for mr brie's report.
mr president, as shadow rapporteur on the set plan, i warmly welcome this initiative. we are establishing a new energy research agenda for europe, which is much needed in view of the challenges we shall be facing in the next decade. the commission believes that europe should lower the costs of clean energy and put industry at the forefront of the low-carbon technology sector. while i agree with these objectives, i would also say that the best intentions never become reality without proper financing. this is why i regret that the commission did not publish the communication on financing for new low-carbon technologies. how does the commission intend to finance these actions? in any case, let me assure you that parliament will not accept the reallocation of funds from the seventh framework programme or the cap. this question of financing is also raised in regard to the 12 ccs projects. while i believe this technology might help industry to reduce co2 emissions, i cannot accept that european taxpayers’ money be used to finance the development of a ccs infrastructure that will be someone’s business in the end. as a liberal, i believe we have to let the market function and develop, if needed, a fair partnership with the industry.
i would like to thank the rapporteurs for their long-term strategic approach to the question of natural gas in the european union and energy research. the european union imported 62% of its gas in 2006, and its demand for and dependence on imported gas will increase to 80% by 2030. it is therefore important to find concrete answers to the questions of ensuring the energy security of the european union and the efficient functioning of the energy market. three elements seem to me to be essential in the rapporteurs' proposals. first, as rapporteur on black sea cooperation, i would like to stress the importance of the successful development of regional cooperation and cross-border interconnection. the regional dimension is the appropriate framework to establish common rules and principles and to ensure coordination and transparency in the gas sector. secondly, it is essential to extend the application of these rules to third country companies active in the energy sector in the european union. finally, i fully support the idea of strengthening the scientific research sector in the field of energy as a key element of that long-term policy.
the union needs a common energy policy. priority projects, such as nabuco, which have also been recognised by the european council, will diversify the european union's natural gas supply sources and must be realised. regional cooperation is essential for ensuring the security of energy supply of the union. that is why i believe and have requested, by way of an amendment, that the geographical area covered by each regional cooperation structure be defined by the commission only after consultation with the member states in that geographical area. i also asked, in an amendment, that for any natural gas pipeline project crossing the union's neighbouring seas, the commission and the member states concerned should carry out an environmental impact study. i consider it essential that the public service obligations and the resulting common minimum standards be better consolidated to ensure that gas services can be affordable to the general public and to small and medium-sized enterprises.
we are debating today three reports of importance to the union's energy policy, which refer to energy technology, energy security and the fight against energy poverty as key factors in achieving energy and climate change objectives. the report by mr paparizov defines a new concept of access to the natural gas transmission networks; the report by mr la russa makes an important contribution to the definition of the medium- and long-term strategy for the internal market in natural gas; and the report by mr buzek stresses the need to develop strategic energy technologies. the swift implementation of these reports will develop a more efficient and transparent internal market with direct effects on increasing competitiveness, price transparency to the end user and consumer protection. it is now time for the commission and the council to encourage explicitly and concretely the diversification of sources of supply and the creation of new gas storage capacities to ensure the union's energy independence and security. i would like to conclude by congratulating the three colleagues on the way they have handled the reporting.
mr president, let me place the matter at issue in a larger political perspective. today energy is almost synonymous with foreign policy and tends to relegate even climate change to a secondary position. it is evident that the current situation has caught europe off-guard. our national energy systems are parochial, monopolistic, complicated and obscure. consequently the tendency to try to manage current challenges individually is irresistible. thus efforts to create a single integrated energy market are increasingly resisted and europe’s objective to reduce its dependency on foreign supply sources becomes almost unreachable. equally, attempting to integrate new solutions in old frameworks would only make our task even more difficult. therefore europe urgently needs to overhaul the current arrangements, push decisively for a single energy market and start investing massively in research on alternative sources of energy. for europe this is simply a matter of survival.
i would like to congratulate the three rapporteurs and at the same time say that romania has acted in full accordance with the requirements of creating the single market for natural gas, by completely separating, including from the point of view of ownership, the transport activity from the activity of production and distribution of natural gas. unfortunately, we do not yet have a competitive single market for natural gas in the european union, and some member states are very reluctant to make this separation between production and distribution. the absence of a single market for natural gas allows some major natural gas suppliers to negotiate supply contracts differently with each member state, sometimes imposing or trying to influence political decisions. i therefore believe that these directives must be adopted as soon as possible and fully implemented.
one solution to energy-efficient and less polluting community transport is the development of modern rail transport, both for passengers and freight. as regards the railway safety directive, i think it is necessary to remove heritage, museum or tourist railways from the scope of the directive. it is also essential that all entities in charge of maintenance are certified and carry out maintenance themselves or can contract it to other maintenance workshops. the entity in charge of maintenance should establish, for the basic components or sub-assemblies intended for railway systems, the basic technical parameters and characteristics with regard to maintenance and logistics in order to comply, during their operation, with the conditions laid down in this directive. the european railway agency has a key role to play in the introduction of ertms by 2020. in order to encourage the investments necessary for the interoperability of the union's rail transport systems, it is essential to stabilise the final version of ertms for a certain period. i would like to draw attention to the need to guarantee european citizens the safety of rail transport. i believe that both the member states and the commission should finance more for the development of rail infrastructure and the modernisation of rolling stock. i ask the commission to give more support to new member states whose rail systems require substantial investment. the tran committee has proposed that ertms be made mandatory for gradual deployment in the trans-european transport network (ten-t) and that the granting of european funds be made conditional on the mandatory use of ertms.

urban policy is not the responsibility of the european union, but of local and regional authorities, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. however, the degree of urbanisation in the union is continuously increasing. over three hundred million citizens live in cities, and the share of the urban population will exceed 80% by the year 2020. urbanization and agglomeration have become a european problem because they affect the well-being of all european citizens. we are seeing in real terms an increased demand for new and diversified modes of transport, which is leading to increased energy consumption, increased land use, and a progressive deterioration in air and soil quality. although there are major differences in national legislation on urban transport and spatial planning, the community institutions can be actively involved in coordinating sustainable urban development and, in particular, urban transport services and can work to ensure the effective dissemination of good practice. mr rack gives us vivid examples of solutions provided by modern technologies such as virtual mobility, but also by the consistent application of multimodality, the optimisation of infrastructure use, the use of alternative modes of transport. education and private initiative are essential to a green europe of cities, and community policies as a whole must take account of all the long-term costs and provide relevant suggestions, effective interregional and crossborder cooperation mechanisms and the necessary information resources. the structural and cohesion funds, which are largely the main cause of urbanisation, must become, through their judicious use at local and regional level, the most effective and readily available resource for solving this challenge facing europe in the 21st century.
i congratulate mr rack on his report. the union needs a new culture of urban mobility, in which public transport and cycling must become more important. the development of public transport requires policies at local, regional or national level for the partial or full subsidisation of public transport services for certain categories of people such as pupils, students, pensioners, disabled people. i consider it necessary that urban development and planning be carried out in an integrated manner, taking into account also current and future needs in the field of urban transport. the introduction of high-speed trains connecting the city centre to river and rail stations, airports and especially to peripheral regions should be a priority in the development and modernisation of large cities. locations with access to an inland waterway can develop intermodal transport to reduce pollution from road traffic in large cities. intelligent transport systems and the development of green areas must be integrated into the new urban mobility policy.
in writing. a new approach to urban mobility is, in my view, essential in the modern city. economic growth in the 1950s and 1960s led to the spread of the horizontal city model in europe, with its population moving away from the centre to the suburbs. but this model, fostered by the proliferation of the car, is no longer sustainable today, in the context of unprecedented fuel prices and concern about global climate change, among which the internal combustion engine is a major source of pollution. initiatives that would enable european cities to plan efficient public transport systems that respect the environment and are accessible to all are welcome, as is the integration into urban planning of alternative modes of transport, whether they are short-distance or varied depending on the time of day. another challenge is urban freight transport, which is essential to the city's economic well-being. this is why i think it is important to implement practices such as exchanges of experience between european city administrations, european-wide urban optimisation databases, and to encourage citizens to change the way they approach personal transport in urban environments.
madam president, i wish to commend the rapporteur on his work. an annual report can speak volumes about achievements and also about policy intricacies and trade-offs. the current inflation rates in europe are tormenting policymakers and citizens. the european central bank has built up its credibility through consistent policies. this performance has been enhanced by this inflation import on the wave of globalisation and the asian economic rise. unfortunately, a reverse situation is under way nowadays because of huge energy and food price rises which reflect the increasing scarcity of available resources. the cost-push pressure is straining markets worldwide. the inflation rate in the euro area is at its highest level for 10 years. this is very worrying, and stagflation also seems to be around the corner. moreover, the financial crisis has complicated the european central bank’s task enormously. the ecb has to fight inflation tenaciously, and anchoring inflation expectations is key in this regard. but the risks are high. it is not clear how long the exogenous cost-push will last. it is critical that a wage price spiral be averted. as we used to talk about inflation moderation in the past decade, so we should strive to achieve moderation of price and wage dynamics in the period to come. more economic divergence in the euro area, which would not foster a good climate for the european central bank’s moves. in addition, when markets are increasingly global, what the european central bank does has to be examined in relation to what other major counterparts do. here it is about interest-rate differentials and overall policy stances. a final note. the grave systemic risks financial markets carry nowadays demand better supervision frameworks, better coordination among the ecb, the fed and other major central banks. the dangers of too-easy-money policies are to be underlined in this regard.
the european central bank is working to ensure price stability amid high uncertainty and inflationary pressures. we do not yet know whether the current level of energy and food prices is the one on which the whole price structure will be based, nor do we know what public policy measures member states will take to facilitate the process of adjustment of businesses and economies and households to the new price structure. the financial crisis is also far from over. as a member of the european parliament, i appreciate the competence and integrity of the european central bank's monetary policies and the determination of its president to stay on target of inflation which characterises the measure of price stability. i express my confidence in the good judgment of the european central bank, in the integrity and independence of the european central bank and in the reluctance of politicians to interfere in the decisions of this bank.
in writing. – as regards economic developments, the fundamentals of the euro-area economy remain sound due to investment growth and improved employment rates and labour-force participation. while moderating, growth in the world economy is expected to remain resilient, benefiting in particular from continued robust growth in emerging economies. with regard to price developments, annual hicp inflation has remained well above the level consistent with price stability since last autumn, reaching 3.7% in may 2008 and – according to eurostat’s flash estimate – 4.0% in june. this worrying level of inflation rates results largely from sharp increases in energy and food prices at the global level in recent months. the uncertainty surrounding this outlook for economic activity remains high and downside risks prevail. in particular, risks stem from the dampening impact on consumption and investment of further unanticipated increases in energy and food prices. moreover, downside risks continue to relate to the potential for the ongoing financial market tensions to affect the real economy more adversely than anticipated. in these circumstances the decision taken by the ecb to raise by 25 basis points to 4.25% the minimum bid rate on the main refinancing operations of the eurosystem is welcome and should be congratulated!
we have often spoken of the purely technical nature of this regulation. in fact, it was a misconception that obscures a deeply political aspect. we have the european union as a single market, but 27 different social security systems. millions of citizens work in countries other than their own and must enjoy the legal social rights that belong to them and their families. institutions need to manage this situation and providers need to discount their services. the rules on which we are dealing with today predate the internet, when the union had six member states with sedentary citizens. today, there are 27 inhabited by citizens who tend to become migrants. modernisation, simplification and adaptation of these rules to the new reality was absolutely necessary. that is the aim of regulation 883/2004, but it cannot be applied without procedures. we are in 2008, four years behind schedule, both for the employees who are claiming their rights and for the efficiency of the companies and institutions involved. there's a saying that "the devil is in the details". today we must congratulate the reporters jean lambert and emine bozkurt because, by solving the problem of detail, we expect a flow of information, with data security and more efficient coordination. the new social agenda proposes these days minor improvements against a background of major shortcomings. the enforcement of regulation 883 is good news. it only slightly mitigates the feeling that the european social agenda has been stagnating in recent years.
the rules on the coordination of social security systems are closely linked to the principle of free movement of persons and should improve the living standards and employment conditions of citizens living in another member state of the european union. the regulation as amended by the rapporteurs simplifies all these procedures and extends its scope to all categories of citizens, both those in employment and those without a job. european citizens must be able to enjoy pension rights in the full amount corresponding to their length of service. once they settle in another eu country, citizens need to find an administrative system capable of collecting all the information on past employment and financial rights arising from their professional activity. that is why i would have liked the commission's proposal to include as precise a solution as possible for how member states can effectively transfer information on social rights. furthermore, i consider this regulation to be fundamental to european labour mobility. a eurobarometer survey shows that more than 50% of citizens are discouraged by the social insecurity they expect to experience as a result of moving to another member state. as a result, only 2% of european citizens currently live in a member state other than the one of which they are a national. if we want mobility to be a real engine of the european economy, we must remove all administrative barriers to the portability of social rights.
in writing. - i voted for the lambert report because it is a response to the needs of the citizens. we live in a world of globalisation where thousands of people work in a country other than their country of residence, we need a coordination of social security systems for all people exercising their right to work in other countries, to guarantee and support mobility which is a fundamental right in the european union. europe allows us to move freely, but it must also give us more social rights, which do not have to stop at national borders. in the hope that european citizens will be able to benefit from social security equality of treatment and non-discrimination i support the initiative to facilitate the freedom of movement of workers. all barriers to mobility must be removed.

mr president, the irish setback to the lisbon treaty has provided enlargement sceptics with an unexpected opportunity: the eu has to stop considering new members, because there is simply no room for them. of course, in strict legal terms, this is true at the moment, but, at the same time, we should make a clear distinction between the lisbon treaty and enlargement. firstly, because the rationale for the treaty has not been enlargement per se but the adaptation of the eu to a globalised context and, secondly, because enlargement is a political rather than a strictly legal matter. enlargement is a power ingredient showing attractiveness and authority as well as the absorption capacity – things we do not miss a chance to claim for our union. therefore, strategic planning, actual negotiations and new initiatives in relation to further enlargement should continue in parallel to the efforts to ratify the lisbon treaty.
enlargement has proved to be one of the european union's most powerful political instruments, serving the union's strategic interests of stability, security and conflict prevention. this has contributed to greater prosperity, growth opportunities, and vital transport and energy corridors. the enlargement policy of the european union has been a success for the european union and for europe as a whole. in this context, it is important to keep the door open to both candidate and potential candidate countries and those with european perspectives in the east of the continent, subject of course to the fulfilment of the criteria and commitments required by them. but to continue enlargement we need a reliable solution for the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. in writing. the prospect of south east european countries joining the european union is driving reforms towards democratic transformation in these countries. the commission's 2007 enlargement strategy paper must send a clear signal of firm commitment to countries with which accession negotiations have started or with which accession prospects are in sight. this is the case, inter alia, of serbia and the republic of moldova. for the latter, romania is a window through which moldovan citizens can maintain hope in a more democratic and prosperous european future. a future accession to the european union is an impetus for the democratic opposition in the republic of moldova to continue the fight for the establishment of democratic legislative and institutional structures, a process that the eu has committed itself to encouraging. the need for internal institutional reforms in the eu, through the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, cannot be a precondition and a pretext for blocking the enlargement of the union.
in writing. eu enlargement has always been only a matter of time and of the compatibility of the political and economic systems between the member countries. a brief review of the 2004 and 2007 enlargement process shows a stronger and more dynamic union both internally and externally, demonstrating that the enlargement process has been beneficial both for the union and for the new countries, but also that we are only adding values within the union, not problems. the political and economic context, european and global, is probably not the most favourable for rapid enlargement, but this should not prevent us from preparing, developing and even reforming enlargement strategies and mechanisms. the western balkan countries, moldova, ukraine and turkey are countries that have expressed interest in joining the eu and enjoy privileged partnerships with the eu, but also have to work internally on compliance with european standards, democracy, stability and prosperity. in this context, i congratulate mr brok on the balance and pragmatism of his report and i hope that a solution will be found quickly to enable all the member states to ratify the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur on the objectivity with which he has expressed the european parliament's position on the commission's 2007 enlargement strategy paper. with each enlargement, the european community has become stronger, and the enlargement process itself has been a success for all member states. the european union has made an astonishing evolution through the institutions and policies it has developed both internally and externally, but especially through the promotion of harmonisation in areas such as economic, social and legal. the union also faces a number of problems which demonstrate the need for each enlargement to be followed by an appropriate consolidation and reassessment of its policies, thus avoiding situations where countries at the centre move towards deeper integration while others remain on the periphery. i support the rapporteur's view that the eastern states should be encouraged to create a common policy area focusing on economic, trade, energy, transport, environment, rule of law, justice and security. by encouraging such projects, the black sea region could become a pole of development and economic growth that would not only promote the welfare of the states in the area, but also the stability and peace on the eastern border of the european union.

more than 40 countries have abolished the death penalty since 1990, and more than 120 states now have a law against it. at european level, the european convention on human rights, which contains an article 2 on the right to life and a protocol 6 to article 1 'abolition of the death penalty', states that no one may be sentenced to such a penalty or executed. the world has seen statistics that are shocking. over 1591 people were executed in 2006, over 3861 people were sentenced to death in 55 countries. i believe that no man has been given the right to take the life of his fellow man. how can you take something that doesn't belong to you? in my mind, i cannot conceive of such a thing, especially since it has been found that in countries where the death penalty is in force, such sanctions do not reduce the number of serious crimes. we propose to change the sentence from death to imprisonment.
with the russian parliament's recognition of the independence of south ossetia and abkhazia, the settlement of the nistru conflict over the transnistrian issue enters a new stage. it is clear to all of us that russia's foreign policy has taken a new turn with this decision of the russian parliament and that is why a repositioning at the level of the whole union is necessary to take account of this reality. given that the issue of transnistria, an area close to the eastern border of the european union, is of marked interest to all member states and in particular to romania, i believe that decisive involvement at community level is necessary to avoid unnecessary strain on relations between states and entities that have declared interests in the area. since natalia timakova, spokeswoman for dmitry medvedev, announced that more meetings would be held with the participation of all interested parties, including representatives from tiraspol, it would not be unimportant to examine here the possibility of setting up a committee to define and present the community's position on the matter. a recent study by the european council on foreign relations reveals that, following the events in georgia, the negotiations for the moldova-transnistria agreement will be much tougher.
mr president, georgia is not just another international crisis to which the eu has to respond. it signals russia’s military comeback, heralded by its offensive energy supply policy initiated in 2006. the eu is caught between principles and economic interests. upholding the former would imply a readiness to sacrifice the latter. conversely, giving priority to the latter would imply a major loss of face. in its turn, russia is equally caught between the profits from its energy sales to the west and respect for international legality. the latter cannot be disrespected with impunity. that is the message our leaders should convey to moscow loudly and clearly. it would be a major waste for the entire international community if russia chose to invest its newly-acquired energies in a futile attempt to restore the bipolar world, instead of associating itself with shaping the new, multipolar, globalised one.
i'll talk about the blocking of sapard payments to romania and its effects in the short and medium term. a european commission mission in june 2008 visited bulgaria and romania and ordered the suspension of payments in sapard projects. corrective action was requested for procedures that are considered non-compliant and in romania the authorities directly involved and responsible proposed a corrective action plan which was accepted. the difficulties are just beginning, though. national payments will resume, probably in september, with the implementation of payment procedures, with the assurance that they are compliant by an independent audit, which can take a year, and with the major risk that the money may be lost permanently, unfortunately in an area that was heavily affected by floods this summer. if the 12 previous audit missions have not found irregularities, if the shortcomings are not fundamental, i wonder and i ask the european commission whether the savings to the agricultural budget are sometimes more important than the sapard projects and their results. i see only one solution, and that is to accept the extension of the term for another year.
rapporteur. − madam president, conceiving of the european union as an area of freedom, security and justice would be nothing but a remarkable goal without the involvement of the already-established european agencies, whose capacities to act and react to combat organised cross-border crime should become stronger. i should like to thank the shadow rapporteurs, with whom i have worked very well on nearly all aspects of this report, and also the president of eurojust and his team for their openness during this process. while drawing up this report, i heard many colleagues call for a european prosecutor. in this respect, i am much more in favour of harmonisation and the setting-up of a european justice system than of reinforcing cooperation. however, for a number of reasons we are, for the time being, still pretty far from such a goal: firstly, because there is no european legislation addressing the issue of jurisdiction in cases that are the competence of eurojust; secondly, because of the reluctance shown by member states even to transfer some of their investigative powers to a european agency. the text on the possibility of eurojust’s national members being part of a joint investigation teams provides a good example. it is a paradox that while the members of the european parliament are ready to truly address serious cross-border crime – including by granting more powers to eurojust, with our major concern being respect for human rights – the member states are preaching one thing but legislating in another. it is difficult to explain to european citizens how we can establish an area of freedom, security and justice if member states do not sufficiently trust our own european agencies. we as a parliament understand and agree with the fact that eurojust must work 24 hours a day, seven days a week. the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs has also agreed that in order for eurojust to be efficient it is essential for its national members to have the same judicial powers they enjoy in their own countries. it also voted in favour of strengthening relations with europol and the european judicial network, and of creating links with other european and international agencies, such as frontex, interpol and the world customs organisation. what we as members of this parliament require – and the report is a reflection of this approach – is a proper balance between the powers of eurojust and those of its national members, on the one hand, and the rights of the defendant, on the other. that is why several of the amendments i have tabled aim to increase the level of protection of procedural rights, such as the right to defence, the right to a fair trial, the right to be informed and the right to judicial redress. at the same time, although we are aware of the strong data-protection system established by the agency, several amendments represent additional safeguards. however, a major concern still exists about data transmitted to third countries and international organisations, because the truth is that we do not know, in reality, what will happen to this data. therefore, in order to make sure that our own european standards are observed, i propose setting up an evaluation mechanism. i should like to thank commissioner barrot for mentioning this. last but not least, i am concerned about the role that the european parliament should play in relation to eurojust. not knowing what the fate of the lisbon treaty will be makes things even more worrisome. however, there is nothing in current community law to prevent parliament from playing an active role in supervising the activities of eurojust. it is entirely a matter of political will, and i truly hope that this house will be allowed to do its job.
on behalf of the ppe-de group. the freedom of movement of european citizens unfortunately also makes it easier and faster for criminals to move around. crossborder crime has thus increased and the legal system must and will continue to adapt to the new situation. i have thus seen the need to harmonize the laws of the member states and, especially during this period, the need for rapid and effective information to the competent authorities of the member states. this report is clearly a step forward in addressing these challenges facing european citizens and institutions. the modernisation of the european judicial network will provide an adequate response to cross-border crime. the report, which was voted unanimously in the libe committee, makes the european judicial network more efficient, making it able to provide the necessary information permanently and from anywhere in the member states. the beneficiaries of this modernisation will be european citizens, who will realise that national legal institutions have the means to react quickly, through a modern and secure telecommunications network. both eurojust and the judiciary in the member states will be able to rely on the structure of the european judicial network, with no one able to find excuses for not having the necessary information. as shadow rapporteur for the people's group, i would like to thank rapporteur silvia-yvonne kaufmann for her work and for the way in which we have managed to find compromise solutions.
first of all, i'd like to congratulate the reporters. in recent years, the work of the european judicial network and eurojust has proved to be extremely important and useful in the field of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the adoption of the council decision on the european judicial network and the decision on the strengthening of eurojust are necessary to make the two structures more and more rapid, given that the mobility of persons and cross-border crime have increased greatly in recent years. the two structures must cooperate and complement each other. the creation of a contact point as a national correspondent for the coordination of the work of the european judicial network, as well as the creation of a national eurojust coordination system, are important for a permanent mutual information and for the orientation of national authorities to either the judicial network or eurojust, depending on the characteristics of the cases handled. structured and timely information is essential for the efficiency of eurojust's work. increased attention should be paid to the establishment of the dedicated communication network for the transmission of personal data. ensuring an adequate level of data protection in the work of the two structures is of the utmost importance.

rapporteur. − madam president, i should like to say a few words in my capacity as a shadow rapporteur on the other two reports and to thank mrs kaufmann for the way we worked together, and mr frança for his work. there were 57 compromise amendments in his report, which says something about the level of work we put in. concerning the report on decisions rendered in absentia, probably the most sensitive aspect relates to the fact that, in some member states, when judgments are rendered in the absence of the defendant, the solution is to have a retrial, thus fully respecting the european convention on human rights (protocol no 7, article 2) and the international covenant on civil and political rights, whereas other countries recognise only the right to an appeal. unfortunately, the proposal in this report is not about harmonising current legislation in the 27 member states. although we should aim at having a european legislation in the future, for the time being we have done our best, at least by ensuring that even in the appeal the defendant enjoys the procedural guarantees as provided for by articles 5 and 6 of the european convention on human rights. i should like to conclude by saying that the good functioning of the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions requires a high level of mutual confidence between the member states, and this confidence must be based on a common observance of human rights and fundamental principles.
in writing. this regulation responds to the need to secure and strengthen the european union's borders by making checks at external border crossing points more efficient. the most important aspect, however, is the establishment of common rules for the harmonisation of the visa information system. although some member states have considered that the mandatory use of the vis would only be feasible when technological development would allow reliable use of portable devices with rapid transfer and secure verification, they consider that the rapporteur's proposal to leave the consultation of the visa information system to the discretion of the border guard is a solution until the technological system allows rapid data transfer and systematic use of the data. it should also be borne in mind that adequate control at eu borders would enhance the internal security of the member states and therefore combat fraud such as organised crime and even acts of terrorism. furthermore, in addition to significantly increasing the efficiency of border controls, systematic consultation of the visa information system would also be a precondition for greater flexibility when applying for a visa.
mr president, the main problem we are facing does not concern the answer to the question of who is right and who is wrong; who is the aggressor or who is the victim; what is a sovereign right and what is a disproportionate reaction. the real problem is that we have no real means to impose a status quo ante or to exert efficient pressure on a country like russia to revise a certain policy. moreover, we cannot ask russia to observe any provision of international law which we have not already breached before. a world in which every crisis is dealt with on a sui generis basis is not a world of order, but of disorder. what we see around us today is not the beginning of a new cold war, but the end of the unipolar order. it is a geopolitical confrontation at global level which takes place within an unregulated international environment where the unilateralists are clashing. when the unipolar order is dead and the multipolar order is not yet born, anarchy and the rule of might prevail. the only reasonable thing we must do is to convene an international conference for security and cooperation, where all the global and regional players, together with the local stakeholders, should negotiate and redefine and reinvent the principles of international law in international relations, the role and powers of international organisations, the procedure for dealing with local crises and the system of security guarantees which could meet the specific opportunities, challenges and dangers of our times. meanwhile, we must accelerate the process of economic integration, political association and institutional approximation with our eastern neighbours such as ukraine and moldova. let us hope that the european union will be up to these expectations.
