mr president, georgia is not a simple episode in international politics. it is the beginning of a chain reaction with important consequences. first, it indicates russia’s military comeback, which will have to be reflected in the new european security strategy under preparation. second, this apparent reconquista indicates russia’s desire to use its newly acquired energies in making good its losses from the 1990s and pay back for the accompanying humiliation, rather than willingness to contribute to the shaping of the future world. third, it highlights the weak position of europe due to increasing energy dependence on russia and the delay in ratification of the lisbon treaty. fourth, it can either restore or further damage transatlantic unity. fifth, it demonstrates that international legality needs to be strengthened both in concept and in respect. sixth, it makes clear that the black sea area needs much more attention and involvement from the eu and therefore that it requires more than a simply synergy.
in writing. as rapporteur for the black sea region, i have always stressed the major challenge that unresolved conflicts pose to regional stability, and the need for a firm and deep eu involvement in the aforementioned area. russia's actions in georgia are regrettable, dangerous in the context of regional and european stability and, by implication, unacceptable to the international community. it is therefore imperative and urgent that the eu move from promises to deeds, to show firmness both in its actions in georgia and in reviewing its relations with russia. in order to ensure stability in the black sea region, three key principles must guide eu action. first, respect for georgia's territorial integrity and international law must be at the heart of any decision. secondly, the current formula for managing conflicts in the region must be reviewed in order to accelerate and increase the possibilities of their final resolution. this implies the eu's active involvement in peacekeeping operations in georgia, but also in the management and resolution of other conflicts in the area, in particular the transnistrian conflict. finally, the eu's efforts to ensure its energy security must be stepped up to the maximum, including through the nabucco project.
in writing. the eu has no right to allow a repetition of the georgian scenario in other conflict regions. the events in georgia are a serious test of the eu's capacity to respond and engage in the frozen conflict zones of the former soviet space. it is necessary for the eu to examine the possibility of sending a european union mission of civilian observers to georgia to monitor compliance with the ceasefire agreement. the disproportionate russian response in south ossetia has had a devastating impact on the civilian population as well as on infrastructure, and constitutes a flagrant violation of international norms. this clearly indicates the need to strengthen security by the presence of multinational and impartial peacekeeping forces. the eu must also give serious thought to a more consistent process of cooperation with moldova and to the possibility of offering, under certain conditions, a much clearer european perspective for chisinau in terms of its guarantee of democratic standards. in order to strengthen good relations and avoid conflict situations, regional cooperation between the black sea littoral states must take a form of multidimensional cooperation that is institutionalised, for example by creating the union of the black sea littoral states.
in writing. mr president of the european parliament, mr president of the council of the european union, madam commissioner, dear colleagues, allow me to convey my condolences to both the russian and georgian citizens who lost their loved ones in this stupid conflict and to assure them of my deepest sympathy. history makes me speak to you today as a european citizen with deep roots in both russia and georgia, as a citizen who is found in european diversity and less so in european unity. we focus on the energy situation in europe, russia's "imperialist" position and georgia's nationalism and lack of diplomacy, but we forget that people and, above all, hopes have died in this conflict. i believe that more than ever we must find ourselves today in a beneficial and constructive unity, in a diplomatic and national balance to face the great challenges that await future generations. in conclusion, i ask the russian president, the president of georgia and the president of the council of the european union to take all the necessary steps to bring this regional conflict to an end as soon as possible and to relaunch a policy of cooperation which is open, balanced and above all for the benefit of the citizens. thank you, sir.
in writing. the great achievement of today's extraordinary european council meeting is the unity of the member states. we must not end up in a cold war situation again. but the russian federation must receive a unified message from the eu: it must respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states, withdraw its troops from frozen conflict zones, respect the international conventions and treaties it has signed, and not base its foreign policy on its status as an energy supplier. this unity of the member states must also be reflected in the union's future actions: a common energy policy based on the creation of new transport routes using sources different from the current ones, the development of a set of policies in the black sea that is commensurate with the geo-strategic and security importance of the area, and the active involvement and promotion of new mechanisms for resolving frozen conflicts in the area. in this context, the reassessment of the neighbourhood policy is absolutely necessary. countries such as ukraine, moldova, georgia and azerbaijan need to be included in a coherent and accelerated mechanism which, if they meet the necessary requirements, could lead to their future membership of the eu.
in writing. the caucasus crisis is considered by some to have begun with president bush's 2005 speech in riga, announcing the need for a new yalta treaty. he could have said a new treaty of trianon, because the misery of many small nations and countries began not with the treaty of trianon, which ended world war ii, but with the treaty of trianon, which ended world war i. the proposal of the then american president wilson for the self-determination of the peoples remained only a dream. today, in the caucasus crisis, there is talk of the interests of the great powers, of oil, of war, but very little about the right of self-determination of the peoples there. the eu's main task in such conflict situations should be to set an example. eleven of the eu member states provide some form of minority-related autonomy. this is 41% of the eu member states. the goal: national minority policy that sets an example for all eu member states: not 41%, but 100%! the european union, with its exemplary national minority policy, can act more effectively also in the caucasus.
in writing. i think it is very important that at this delicate moment europe stands united and takes a united position on the conflict in georgia. but we must continue to provide assistance and help rebuild the affected areas in georgia, support confidence-building measures and develop regional cooperation. at the same time, europe needs to accelerate the development of european energy projects (such as nabucco and p8). even if the main focus is on georgia, considering the geographical position of azerbaijan, i think we must also take into account the need to establish an eu-azerbaijan partnership to support and continue eu energy projects. i would like to stress that the resolution of the frozen conflicts in the black sea region can only be achieved within the limits and on the basis of international law, with respect for the territorial integrity of states and their sovereignty over the entire territory, as well as with respect for the principle of the inviolability of borders. i support the council's position that the european union is ready to commit itself, including through a presence on the ground, to support all efforts towards a peaceful and lasting solution to the conflict in georgia. i believe that only through dialogue and negotiation can we achieve the desired results.
we hoped that these proposals would help to reduce the social gap between european citizens. unfortunately, the package only puts us in front of another gap, that between some good intentions and the tools needed to achieve them. it also happens where there are european regulations that oblige member states to take measures. one example is the wage discrimination against women in the labour market. there's legislation here, repeated commitments, no improvement in the last eight years. but assuming that employers understand the economic benefits of fair pay and their legal obligations, the difficulties are insurmountable. there is no system of job evaluation on a non-discriminatory basis, which would constitute a common criterion for comparing different activities. without it, the principle of equal pay for work of equal value remains an illusion, as does the reduction of the sectoral gap. occupational classification systems are flawed where they exist. we already have court decisions that admit that, by relying on manual labor, they disregard the different skills needed for the job and create discrimination. the open method of coordination has commendable social objectives, but even indicators measuring some of these objectives are missing from the list of common indicators. the sad conclusion is that disinterest in gender issues is matched only by a lack of political will for effective common labour market regulations.
i would like to bring up some ideas related to the legislative package on the social european agenda. i very much appreciate the european commission's initiatives in this area and those set out in its communication 'building skills for the 21st century - european school-to-school cooperation'. beyond these initiatives, however, i would like to propose to the european commission to launch a pilot project to establish a european scholarship for children from economically and geographically disadvantaged areas. at european level, 19 million children and young people are at risk of poverty and 6 million drop out of secondary education each year. in romania, for example, young people from rural areas and those from mountainous or isolated regions have, according to a eurobarometer survey, a 5% chance of completing university studies. this is a far cry from the european union's target of 85% of young people having access to upper secondary education. member states do not have the financial means to remedy this worrying situation on their own. the european union must therefore fight by every possible means, legislation, funds, european policies, to promote opportunities and access to education for all young people.
i'm glad we're discussing the re-launch of the social package today. europe needs social progress, europe as a whole, with its older and newer members. the united europe faces the same challenges: ageing populations, job losses due to globalisation, poverty among children. i welcome, commissioner špidla, your approach to solidarity between generations. we need a new spirit here, but i also welcome the reiteration of the idea of solidarity between regions, because this is where we measure social cohesion or lack of it most faithfully.
in writing. mr president, against the background of the declarations by the conventions that 2008 will be the year of the relaunch of social europe, the so-called social package is a set of legislative initiatives whose convergence remains for the time being at the desired stage. perhaps it is time to take a more forceful and applied approach to a set of issues whose direct impact on citizens is greater than ever. we must, in fact, take it upon ourselves to ensure that all community citizens enjoy non-discriminatory living and working conditions. firstly, the resumption of discussions on a community minimum wage is not only appropriate but also necessary in this context. secondly, the same applies to the creation of uniform conditions in all eu countries for the community labour market. it is not fair that today the attitude of many eu governments towards european citizens is differentiated according to the eu country of origin. in the same context, the commission's significant initiative to improve the visibility and working methods of the eu social protection and integration strategy and to strengthen its interaction with other policies is also emerging. i have noted with satisfaction the commission's proposal for a horizontal directive on combating discrimination in areas other than employment.
in writing. the lisbon treaty recognises that the union must be based on a social market economy that provides its citizens with access to decent working and living conditions, education, health and social protection services. the union's population is ageing. if in 2007 citizens aged over 65 represented 17% of the union population, by 2030 this percentage will reach 24,6%. the latest eurostat statistics show that from 2015 the number of deaths will exceed the number of births, leading to a decrease in the number of european citizens from 521 million in 2015 to 506 million in 2060. under these conditions, immigration seems to remain the main factor in the growth of the union's population. but migration flows affect member states differently. while ireland experienced a 21.8% increase in population between 1985 and 2007, bulgaria's population declined by 14.4% over the same period. what are the solutions offered by the social package to these challenges? the citizens of the union expect firm measures to create well-paid jobs, to guarantee access to quality education, health and social protection services. the social package is the insurance policy for the future of the union and is essential for its long-term development.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to reduce the decision-making time for the award of european funding through the culture 2007-2013 programme. experience of the past years has shown that the procedure for awarding funds through this mechanism is quite slow and european cultural operators may have financial problems as a result. given that cultural institutions and artists applying for these funds are generally in a delicate financial situation, i believe that any measure to facilitate access to european funds is welcome.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs katerina batzeli for several reasons. it is well known that education and training are key priorities for the european union in achieving the lisbon objectives. the aim of the lifelong learning programme must be to maintain a flexible, self-reliant, knowledge-based society with quantitative and qualitative economic and cultural development, all in line with and in the spirit of (more) stronger social cohesion. this is why continuing training must involve all social factors. of course, like any programme of this size, it must be clear, coherent, monitored and regularly evaluated after each stage of implementation to allow for (re) adjustments, in particular as regards the priorities for implementing the measures. however, continuing training programmes should also target people in their mature years. the fact that the emphasis is often on early education, followed by the capping of the individual, means that every citizen must be stimulated and motivated to participate in a form of continuing learning that ensures potential placement in the labour market, regardless of age. this is all the more important when we also refer to statistics on the ageing of the labour force and the decline in the active population.
in writing. − europe as a whole is today facing a series of essential and dramatic changes for citizens of all ages. the importance of education and training in the lisbon strategy for growth and jobs was recognised, with the european council repeatedly stressing the role of education and training in the long-term competitiveness of the european union. today we can no longer expect people to stay in the same industry or in the same place for their entire lives. their career paths will be unpredictable and they will need a wide range of general skills to be able to adapt. to prepare them for life and society, schools need to guide them towards lifelong learning, a comprehensive european union programme that sees people able to learn at any age, and thus remain active and living members of society. that is why i voted for this report with all my heart, because we need to develop programmes for these people, particularly in the newly joined countries.
in writing. − the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part, entered into force on 1 july 1999, before the enlargement of the european union to include the republic of bulgaria and romania. the protocol to the pca was to be drawn up to allow the new member states (romania and bulgaria) to accede to this agreement. i think that parliament should have more initiatives of this kind, taking into account the partnerships signed with other countries in the region. the situation in the region makes it necessary to establish a partnership between the european union and azerbaijan this year, giving europe the opportunity to continue its energy projects. azerbaijan should receive special attention from the european union, also on the basis of the fact that it has a very balanced policy in the region and that it is willing to contribute to the implementation of the european union's energy projects.
in writing. − mutual recognition is the 'cornerstone' of judicial cooperation at european level and any clarification of the instruments for implementing this principle is welcome. the decision passed today is welcome. but i would like to draw attention to another issue, namely the way in which some member states are putting in place important instruments such as the european arrest warrant. in january 2007, the romanian authorities issued a european arrest warrant for czech citizen františek priplata, who was sentenced to eight years in prison for incitement to commit aggravated murder in the 2000 murder of a romanian trade union leader. the czech republic, on whose territory the sentenced person is located, however, applies the surrender procedure only for acts committed after 1 november 2004. as a result, eight years after the crime, the convict has not yet been extradited and has not begun to serve his sentence. i believe that member states which agree to apply judicial cooperation instruments in this way should seriously consider whether to maintain these reservations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the armando frança report on the application of the principle of mutual recognition to confiscation orders and the 2008 framework decision. /.../jha on the application of the principle of mutual recognition to judgments in criminal matters imposing custodial sentences or measures for the purpose of their enforcement in the european union. there are increasing cases of dangerous criminals taking advantage of freedom of movement and the abolition of borders within the european union to avoid prosecution. i support this report unconditionally because it provides for a uniform regulation on 'in absentia' sentences, a regulation which is particularly necessary to avoid the possible blockage of the judicial system by those who flee justice from one country to another in the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the brejc report today because the use of the vis (visa information system) is of fundamental importance for the effectiveness of external border controls. the visa information system should be systematically consulted by border police officers for any visa holder in order to ensure border security. the enlargement of the schengen area has removed barriers within the european union. third-country nationals are still only checked once at the entrance. 50% of illegal immigrants enter the eu legally, but overstay because there is no visa control system. we want europe to be safer, but at the same time welcoming to those who come for tourism or business. the amendment voted in the european parliament today is in favour of eu citizens and third country nationals who do not need a visa, as it would considerably reduce congestion at land border crossing points.
in writing. − asylum laws and practices still differ between member states, and asylum seekers are treated differently from one country to another. unless a satisfactory and uniform level of protection is achieved throughout the european union, the dublin system will always produce unsatisfactory results, both technically and humanly, and asylum seekers will continue to have good reasons to address their application to a particular member state in order to benefit from the most favourable decisions at national level. the high number of multiple applications and the low number of transfers carried out indicate weaknesses in the dublin system and the need to create a common european asylum system. the implementation of the dublin regulation may result in unequal distribution of responsibility for persons seeking protection to the detriment of member states that are particularly exposed to migratory flows solely because of their geographical location. the commission's assessment shows that in 2005, the 13 member states at the external borders of the union faced increasing challenges as a result of the application of the dublin system, so that the first country of entry criterion provided for by the dublin system put the member states at the external borders in a very difficult situation.
the rapporteur for the opinion of the imco committee. - madam president, honourable members, commissioner, honourable ministers, i would like to congratulate the rapporteurs involved in the work on the telecom package. i think mrs trautmann's report is a balanced position and i support the compromise amendments proposed. i am also pleased that certain amendments have been accepted, in particular those relating to spectrum harmonisation and certain measures relating to global telecommunications services. european economic growth and consumer welfare depend on a dynamic and competitive telecommunications sector. competitive markets have more broadband available, new entrants have brought increased speeds and innovative services. the telecoms framework directive must be geared towards increased investment; next generation networks must also be considered and consumer choices must be more diversified, leading to lower costs and better services for consumers. in conclusion, i would like to express my confidence in the changes we want to bring to the telecom package, which will benefit consumers by offering them a wider range, lower costs and more diversified services.
the development of the information society is based on electronic communications networks and services. the switchover from analogue to digital television by 2012 will free up a significant spectrum at european level, thus allowing the development of new technologies and innovative solutions that will boost european competitiveness in this sector. in order to fully benefit from the digital dividend in europe, parliament supports a common, flexible and balanced approach to its use, allowing broadcasters to continue and expand their services and electronic communications operators to use this resource to provide new services with important social and economic uses, and stresses that the digital dividend should be allocated in accordance with the principle of technological neutrality. the use of the digital dividend can help to achieve the objectives of the lisbon strategy by providing enhanced interoperable social services such as e-government, e-health, e-learning, especially for those living in disadvantaged, isolated or rural areas. while recognising the right of member states to determine the use of the digital dividend, we argue that a coordinated approach at community level significantly improves the value of the digital dividend and is the most effective way to avoid harmful interference between member states and between member states and third countries, and to ensure that spectrum users benefit from all the benefits of the internal market. consumer confidence in information society services depends on the quality of electronic communications services, their security and the protection of personal data. it is essential that national regulatory authorities ensure that all providers of electronic communications services are consulted before adopting specific measures in the field of security and integrity of electronic communications networks. i also believe that member states should put in place measures to promote the creation of a market for widely accessible products and services that incorporate facilities for disabled users.
president of the council. - madam president, i thank you for allowing me to speak now and i would like to apologize for having to return to paris afterwards. my colleague luc chatel will be answering many of the questions that have been asked. i shall merely say a few words about mr harbour's comments on the lack of debate on the scope of universal service. i would first like to express my agreement with the rapporteur on what he said, that access to broadband is a major issue for our societies, whether it is access to knowledge or essential services. as mr harbour has said, broadband access is not part of the current scope of universal service. the french presidency simply wants to open the debate on how to guarantee access to broadband throughout europe. when listening to the various member states, it is clear that different scenarios can be envisaged. first, the inclusion of broadband in the universal service directive, then the freedom to allow only those member states which so wish to include broadband access in their universal service, and finally an intermediate position, which would be to say that the inclusion of broadband in the scope of the universal service becomes mandatory in the member states when broadband has reached sufficient maturity. so we have the opportunity, together, under the french presidency, to open this debate and try to bring the views closer together, which is what the commission is also trying to do. i would just like to add a word to mrs harms' attention, to say that we are not opposed to the development of the internet and the protection of copyright. in the age of convergence, we must develop containers, networks and content, and therefore foster creativity and authorship. france, as you have recalled, is committed to copyright but the french presidency does not seek to impose the example, which we will promote in france, of prevention and graduated response, what we call the creation and internet law. finally, we are very aware, as you said, of the need to protect both privacy and personal data. we do not see any contradiction between this and other concerns.
mr president, the telecom package is an important step forward in modernising and harmonising telecommunications in europe. i worked on the citizens’ rights directive and, together with the rapporteur, mr harbour, we did a lot of work and we reached consensus on many issues. this directive will ensure better protection of consumer rights in electronic communications. number portability, and privacy protection and security in telecommunications are other examples of improvements brought by this directive. we had a very delicate discussion on network neutrality. my opinion is that extreme network neutrality, as we experienced in some amendments, will make networks more congested, slower, less efficient and more expensive. network management is necessary to run efficient and intelligent networks and to maximise the overall user experience and value. i am very satisfied that we agreed on amendments regarding the emergency number 112 and, after the directive has been adopted, member states will make further efforts to inform and educate the public on the use of 112. the 112 number will be made accessible from the entire eu territory and member states will have to ensure the implementation of caller location. in addition, access to emergency services through 112 may be blocked in case of repeated misuse by the user and 112 will be more accessible to people with disabilities. i also hope that the amendment regarding the establishment of an eu-wide early warning system will be adopted. this amendment does not require an agency in brussels to be set up but the definition of common standards about the warning system to be done jointly by the relevant authorities of the member states. of course, the warning would be launched at the local level, but on the basis of common standards that would ensure that all potentially affected citizens of the eu could get and understand this message and act in a way that will save their lives. i am very sure that the telecom package will support the efforts of companies in improving their performance and investment in new technologies and at the same time will consolidate the consumer rights of european citizens.
the report under discussion provides an opportunity to stimulate, by exploiting the digital dividend, the large-scale use of broadband technologies in rural, isolated or disadvantaged areas, given that there are still many localities where digital technology is completely lacking or where access to digital services is not possible due to a lack of infrastructure. we support the acceleration of the development by lagging member states, such as romania, of national strategies on the digital dividend, which will put into practice measures that will allow citizens to have faster and easier access to interoperable social services, in particular those that allow access to education, vocational training and health systems. we are sounding the alarm about the care that must be taken to ensure the greatest possible transparency in the reallocation of frequency allocations and investments in the new generation of infrastructure, so that all the countries of the european union have access to them.
my dear colleagues, there are some things that are talked about a lot but not done. in the debate on the social package, we spoke about the lack of instruments to apply the principle of equal pay for work of equal value and thus to reduce the pay gap between women and men. without them, commitments are just words, and legislation is useless. there are also issues that are little or nothing done about, but not even talked about. the 100,000 women who are trafficked every year are not talked about much, except here, late at night; probably because they are commodities, not citizens. most are trafficked for prostitution. we call for stronger integrated action against trafficking networks, but also concerted measures to discourage demand for prostitution. without demand, traffic loses its raison d'être. the situation of women who work as housekeepers and domestic workers is not mentioned; they are invisible. with no social rights or minimal rights, they face the same risk of abuse as women in their own families, including the risk of exploitation. for those working in other countries, the lack of political rights is added to the fragility of the social and economic situation. proper regulation of their situation is not just a matter of justice now, it would prevent the high rate of poverty among older women in the future. nor can you talk about women in the government of my country, because they don't exist. commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we believe that the time has come to move from statements about what should be done to doing what is right.
we are talking about the need to combat violence against women, to encourage women's participation in civic life and an aspect that is part of the work of the committee on culture - the discrepancies between the level of education of women and men. while women are better educated than men, the gender pay gap in the labour market continues to be widespread. i myself, as a member of the committee on culture and education, tabled an amendment to the opinion drawn up by cult on this report. i believe it is essential to remove from the media images that depict women in degrading poses, given the impact that the mass media have on public perceptions and attitudes. the european union's policy on gender equality is still a topical issue in western society.
mr president, equality between women and men must be a basic principle of european society. the latest eurobarometer survey indicates that rural women are not involved in decision-making in their communities, do not have a stable job and most of them only take on domestic responsibilities, reaching 98% in some areas. however, over 50% of women want access to the european labour market and a qualification that will help them to get a job in public administration, agriculture, social welfare or education. a significant percentage also want to take advantage of the facilities that exist at european level to start a business. i therefore believe that initiatives by rural women to become actively involved in society, to continuously improve themselves and to participate in the economic development of their area should be supported. eliminating discrimination requires a combined european effort. programmes such as the european social fund and progress in partnership with governments and local authorities need to allocate even more funds to support rural women.
in writing. romania, although in terms of the legislative framework and the number of government initiatives and programmes aimed at reducing gender inequality is among the good students of the european union, suffers from deficiencies in several important aspects that accentuate and perpetuate inequality between women and men. as regards access to management positions for women, romania is among the last places in europe. of the 331 members of the parliament, only 37 are women, just over 11% of the total. the percentage of women in local government in romania is even lower. sweden has almost as many women as men in parliament. in romania, a third of women work part-time, compared with only 7.7% of men, for an average wage 15% below that of men. this is closely related to the persistence of gender stereotypes that make most of the housework fall to women. gender inequality and related prejudices are unfortunately present not only in the family but in the educational framework of romanians themselves. studies show that school activities in romania tend to form gender-differentiated mindsets, as do socioeconomic orientation activities organized by teachers. i therefore stress the importance of including in the report points on the importance of education in eliminating gender inequality.
in writing. i believe that the persistence of discrimination between the sexes is primarily due to outdated mindsets still present in modern societies: the man provides for the family financially, and the woman takes care of her social needs. these attitudes are found in all states, but especially in the underprivileged areas. with proper education, this phenomenon can be eliminated. in this context, i think it is also necessary to take into account the fact that the evolution of present-day society as a whole has led to an increasing involvement of women in working life, with their status in society improving markedly. however, problems may arise at the family level, especially with regard to the care, involvement and education of children. lack of time, busy work schedules, the glamour of strangers, lead to diminished parental control over children during the holidays, as well as between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. during the school activity. therefore, solutions must be identified to eliminate the concern about what the child is doing while the parent is at work by developing activities within or outside schools that provide cover for the lack of parental supervision. basically, to extend the school by school method, which becomes a useful project for the family, the community, the country, europe.
in writing. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and stress the importance of the contents of this report for achieving the objectives of economic growth in the context of the lisbon strategy. both the european union and the member states must provide a better model for society. despite the progress that has been made, inequality between women and men persists and that is why we must act. i want to draw attention to a problem that so many women face every day and for which so few get a favorable verdict, and i'm talking about sexual harassment. according to a national study in romania, 90 percent of sexual harassment victims were women, and 1 in 9 people in urban areas experienced sexual harassment. in over 55% of cases, the abuser was the subject's professional boss. i believe that there is a need to re-evaluate policies and actions in this area with a view to raising living and working standards for women, and that member states must urgently implement community legislation aimed at equal treatment between women and men in the labour market, including with regard to sexual harassment.
in writing. it is time to break down stereotypes and take decisive action to give women and men real equal opportunities. progress has been made over the past decade in increasing the representation of women in european top politics, but it is still insufficient. in contrast, the remuneration discrepancies have remained relatively constant over the past years. european societies are still subject to exclusion and firm decisions, much bolder, and a much more effective media campaign are needed. the overall participation of women in decision-making is also clearly distorted in romania, the only country where not a single woman holds a ministerial post, and women only occupy 9% of the seats in parliament. romanian society has a duty to fight mentalities, gender discrimination in all its everyday forms. i believe in the positive effects of using electoral quotas for women's representation. examples of good practice are found in the nordic countries, but not only. whether it is an electoral system based on proportional representation by guaranteeing gender parity of candidates, but also equal visibility in the media (belgium) or distribution quotas established by law (finland, sweden, spain, france), i believe that in romania the situation of women who want such involvement in political, economic and social life can be greatly improved.
i would like to propose some practical ways in which we can tackle the harmful influence of advertising on gender equality in europe. from the point of view of european legislation in this area, a key point is the principle of country of origin. this is also the case with regard to advertising, so that a production accepted by a national audiovisual council in one member state must be accepted for broadcasting in all the others. we have recently seen clear examples of gender discrimination promoted by advertising productions that could not be stopped from being broadcast in the european union states. i therefore believe that derogations from the country of origin principle should be introduced where it is found that the european pact for gender equality has been breached by offensive media productions. since this is an area of community competence, namely trade in audiovisual services, i believe that fines should be imposed by the european commission on producers who promote discriminatory images through advertising.
in writing. – even if strict conditions are respected and efsa concludes that cloned meat is equivalent to conventional meat, animal cloning for food supply is, to many people, a risky and morally unacceptable practice. the current level of suffering and health problems in cloned animals reinforces that claim. if conventional methods work, then why should we encourage a technique that causes so many animals to suffer and die? it neither improves breeding, nor food safety nor the security of provision. it clearly provides no obvious benefit to the consumer. furthermore, european consumers have, on several occasions, expressed their wish not to have food products from clones or the offspring thereof on their table. it is a legitimate call and sends a clear signal, so why are we even considering cloning for food supply in the first place? people want to have control over what they eat and they are concerned that cloning will ultimately be forced on them. if we do not wish to further alienate the public from the european project, i believe we had better listen to their will and enforce it. therefore, i call for no cloning of animals for food supply.

in writing. the proposal for a decision implementing the globally harmonized system of classification and labelling of chemicals (ghs) is an important step in protecting the environment, consumers who will have more choice and companies looking to enter the international market. harmonised use of labels and uniform description of the hazards of chemicals will increase consumer confidence in such products, while facilitating international trade, as the industry will be able to apply the same labels to all regions where it exports. moreover, the uniform system of classification of substances is an essential factor in guaranteeing the free movement of goods within the internal market. however, we need to ensure that this regulation does not increase the number of tests carried out on vertebrate animals for the purpose of harmonising the classification criteria, but that these tests are only carried out where there are no alternative solutions that guarantee the same level of quality. the global classification system should allow the use of methods that do not involve animal testing, even if their validation involves a lengthy and costly bureaucratic process. since animal testing has never been officially validated, the authentication of alternative tests seems a burden, but research in this area should be encouraged.
in the transport sector, sustained efforts should be made to introduce alternative fuel vehicles on the market that contribute to a significant improvement in urban air quality. common standards for the approval of hydrogen engines are necessary to ensure the safe use of hydrogen for the propulsion of vehicles. the use of hydrogen as a fuel, whether as fuel cells or as internal combustion engines, does not generate carbon emissions or greenhouse gases. type-approval of hydrogen-based vehicles is based on the specification and compliance with the technical requirements of hydrogen-based components. given the characteristics of hydrogen, the vehicles require specific treatment by the rescue services. i would stress the need for member states to invest in the infrastructure necessary for the storage and distribution of alternative fuels, without which the number of less polluting vehicles cannot increase significantly.

president of the council. - mr president, madam commissioner, madam rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by expressing our appreciation for the work done by the parliamentary committees, and in particular by mrs flautre, as chairman of the subcommittee on human rights. this is an important work, because, first of all, the relationship between the use of restrictive measures and human rights is a topical subject which, until recently, has been the focus of the attention of the various actors on the international scene. i think it is worth recalling that, in the context of the common foreign and security policy, one of the objectives of restrictive measures remains the foundation of democracy and the rule of law, as well as respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. however, it is legitimate to ask ourselves, as we do, and as you have done in your report, what the impact of such measures may be on the fundamental rights of the individuals subject to them. that is why, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the council has drawn up a concept paper on restrictive measures entitled 'basic principles on the use of restrictive measures' in which it recalls the attention paid, i quote, 'to full respect for human rights and the rule of law and to full compliance with our obligations under international law'. this commitment is of course still at the heart of our priorities. it should also be borne in mind that the use of restrictive measures is not limited to human rights policy. it is a tool like any other of the common foreign and security policy and there are other objectives besides the defence of human rights, which concern the maintenance of peace and the strengthening of international security, the safeguarding of the fundamental interests and the strengthening of the security of the union or, quite simply, the promotion of international cooperation. sanctions must therefore be part of - as you have stressed - a comprehensive and integrated approach by a country, which includes political dialogue, incentive measures, conditionality and other external policy instruments in parallel, and in this respect i am pleased that the report is in line with the council's view that all the instruments at its disposal, including restrictive measures, should be used flexibly. you will understand that it is not easy to make a comparative analysis by limiting oneself to the different sanctions regimes and using the human rights situation in each country as the sole criterion, and it is important not to take a regime of restrictive measures out of its context, just as when these measures are implemented, it is not, of course, necessary to assume that everything is automatic in this implementation. as regards the implementation of restrictive measures in the fight against terrorism, it is primarily aimed at preventing acts of terrorism, in particular anything that may contribute to the financing of such acts. the lists are known, public, as are the measures they entail. one of the conditions for the sustainability of this system is based on two pillars: the first is that these systems must be credible, which implies that the greatest attention should be paid to updating these lists so that they can reflect reality. the second principle is respect for the rule of law, and therefore for a number of fundamental principles: transparency of procedures, possibilities of appeal and rights of the defence. in this debate, i am sorry to be a little long but it is the current events that are prompting me to do so we must of course take note of the judgment of the court of justice which was delivered this morning and which annuls, with effect from 3 december next, the effects of a community regulation freezing the assets of two applicants pursuant to a security council resolution because they were not able to know the reasons for which they were included on the terrorist lists. what we note is that the court does not forbid the council from taking further measures to freeze funds provided that the persons concerned can have information as to why they are affected by such measures, either at the time when the measure is decided or at least as soon as possible after the decision. we also note that the court's judgment states that the primacy of un security council resolutions in international law is not in question and that it is on this basis that the rules of procedure will be amended by 3 december, after your assembly has been informed. the report by mrs flautre deals more specifically with the mechanism for evaluating sanctions, asking the council to carry out an evaluation or impact study of the union's policy in this area. i would like to stress the council's willingness to do so, and in particular to ensure that experience can be exchanged and that national best practices can be developed in the application of restrictive measures. the experience gained in designing and implementing measures in different contexts continually feeds into every political debate we have in the council, and the council also conducts in-depth discussions on the relevance, nature and anticipated effectiveness of possible sanctions, drawing on the reports drawn up by the heads of mission of the european union and on the observations communicated by the member states. so, on the nature of sanctions, we welcome the convergence of views with the report and in particular the fact that targeted sanctions are favoured over general sanctions, and we have noted that the report calls on the council and the commission to follow a mixed approach - which could be summed up as the carrot and stick approach - which indeed seems to us to be the one that should be adopted. we also agree with the report's analysis of the importance of international cooperation, which is the basis of credibility. we attach particular priority to the work carried out within the framework of the united nations. we are ensuring, within the council, that, on the basis of the un resolutions and the measures decided in the security council, there is alignment with the countries which are closest to the european union. we are also ensuring that the issue of sanctions is also raised in the political dialogue meetings and human rights consultations we have with a number of target countries. finally, in this draft report, the european parliament expresses its wish to be involved at all stages of the process leading to the design, implementation and monitoring of restrictive measures. the council is fully aware of this and welcomes the very keen interest of the european parliament in the union's policy in this area. the council is therefore particularly concerned to ensure that your assembly is kept regularly informed of developments in this field. i would like to end by welcoming the european parliament's commitment in this area and encourage it to make use of all its parliamentary contacts with third countries to improve understanding of the european union's sanctions regime and to examine the possibilities for coordinated action to promote human rights. for all these reasons i welcome the report just presented by mrs flautre.
member of the commission. - mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, madam rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, the commission takes note with interest of the report on the application of sanctions and the evaluation of sanctions in the field of human rights. sanctions are one of the effective instruments available to the european union to promote respect for human rights in third countries and have been applied to this end in belarus, china, myanmar, uzbekistan, the former yugoslavia and zimbabwe, to name a few important cases. the commission welcomes the holding of this debate on the implementation and evaluation of this important instrument of the common foreign and security policy. as the president said, whilst recognising that this policy pursues several objectives, any decision to apply sanctions in the framework of the cfsp must be taken after evaluating and weighing up several objective interests. that is why an assessment of the coherence of sanctions policy must be carried out, not only in the light of the human rights records of third countries, but also taking into account the other objectives and criteria of the cfsp. the systematic and unilateral, almost automatic, application of sanctions against all countries whose policies do not fully respect human rights does not seem desirable. the european union should take into account the impact on relations with the countries targeted by sanctions, which are economic as well as political in nature. however, it is not only the impact on our diplomatic relations that must be taken into account, but also the impact on the international activities of our economic operators. in general, sanctions should be targeted and targeted only at the leaders of the country concerned, while sparing the populations who are already suffering from the violation of human rights. moreover, when sanctions are decided, it should also be decided on the basis of which criteria they can be lifted, an 'exit strategy' while reserving a minimum of flexibility for cases where the third countries concerned meet most but not all of the criteria. i would also like to stress that sanctions are not intended to replace judicial proceedings against those responsible for human rights violations. these crimes are the responsibility of the courts and tribunals, including the international criminal court. on the other hand, sanctions are intended to bring about a change in the policies of a third country, for example, to promote respect for human rights in the legal system of the country concerned. they therefore have a progressive objective and can be repealed as the policies of the country concerned change. the european union, for example, has applied sanctions in support of the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia. we believe it is important to promote respect for human rights in third countries and we are also continuously monitoring the application of human rights in third countries. in each case, the most naturally effective of all the possible instruments should be identified. we therefore believe that a thorough reflection on the application of sanctions in order to promote policies which respect human rights is a useful policy, and i would like to thank you, madam rapporteur, for taking the initiative.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development. − mr president, as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development on this report, i would like to state that the european union should use this remarkable tool of external policy with wisdom and prudence. no matter what the circumstances or the type of sanctions applied, there is always the potential of negative side effects that could generate regrettable situations. i strongly believe that sanctions should apply only when diplomatic persuasion has failed, and, in order to be efficient, the eu must always have a comprehensive assessment of the situation, a coherent strategy and an accurate evaluation of the results. to uphold credibility and avoid the accusation of double standards, the eu has to be able to justify the adoption or non-adoption of sanctions based primarily on human rights grounds and arguments of effectiveness. i think it is crucial that, by imposing sanctions, the european union reveals its strengths and not its weaknesses.
i hope that this report will play an important role in strengthening european policy on the imposition of community sanctions. i think it is essential that in future there should be greater cohesion between member states, both in the decision-making process on sanctions and in their actual implementation. if we want the european union to be a strong and respected presence on the international stage and to have the greatest possible impact from its actions, including sanctions, it is essential that we show as much solidarity as possible and avoid using different units of measurement. it is essential that sanctions affect the population of the states whose political regions are subject to sanctions to a minimum extent. let us not make those peoples suffer twice as long as they are already victims of oppressive regimes or corrupt governments. i am glad that the commissioner has also pointed this out. last but not least, i would like to raise the issue of the appropriateness of sanctions. we have just had a concrete case at the beginning of this week: the georgian crisis and the position of the 27 member states vis-à-vis russia. the results of monday's summit are the subject of heated debate precisely because of the discrepancy between the decided, almost vehement tone of the attitude expressed and the reluctance to resort to sanctions. i believe that as long as things can be rectified and dialogue can prevent the situation from deteriorating, sanctions should remain a measure of last resort.
sanctions are one of the instruments that the union can use to implement its human rights policy. however, as the rapporteur has also noted, the lack of an impact study on the sanctions policy of the european union makes it extremely difficult to measure the effects and effectiveness of this policy on the ground and therefore indicates a lack of transparency, coherence and even legitimacy of the community sanctions. as long as the european union does not speak with one voice in its common security policy, it is very difficult for us to impose effective and systematic community sanctions. it is regrettable that the union and the member states have not made systematic use of sanctions, and i therefore believe, mr president, that a coherent strategy for the policy of applying sanctions, with a view to respecting human rights, is needed, a strategy which takes account of the agreements and clauses already signed, avoiding double standards and thus contributing to increasing the credibility of the union. i congratulate mrs flautre on this report.

in writing. the eu has committed to meeting the millennium development goals, including reducing the maternal mortality rate by 75% by 2015. although eu countries are on the right track overall, progress is slowest in the area of maternal health. the european commission's initiatives to allocate funds to health systems reform to improve the quality of and access to pre- and postnatal services, support research in reproductive medicine and medical staff training were welcomed in order to achieve objective 5. the charter for strengthening sanitary systems adopted in tallinn in june 2008 is also an important step forward. however, there are developed countries like france, the united kingdom, and the netherlands with very low mortality rates, for which the 75% reduction by 2015 seems difficult, because the rate of progress is slower than in countries with higher maternal mortality rates. there are also still disparities in the progress made in eu countries and even in the regions of different countries. achieving the 2015 target therefore requires a rapid modernisation of european health systems with a particular focus on research to improve prenatal and postnatal services, as well as health education and more effective family planning.
in writing. the european union is a strong supporter of the millennium development goals adopted by the united nations, which set targets to be achieved by 2015 in the areas of peace, security, development, governance and human rights. among the eight goals, greater attention should be given to improving maternal health, as over half a million women, mostly in africa and asia, lose their lives during pregnancy or childbirth. the main cause of the increase in the worldwide mortality rate is the lack of skilled personnel to provide maternal care during pregnancy and at birth. this situation must be remedied by investing substantial funds in the underdeveloped countries, both in training specialized personnel and in medical equipment. the targets for romania in improving maternal health are to reduce the mortality rate to 10 deaths per 100,000 newborns by 2015 and to ensure universal access to health services. romania currently has a negative natural rate with a mortality rate of 12‰. through social assistance and information programmes, mother and child services, and additional eu financial support, the birth rate must resume its upward trend and romania must remain in the european union's demographic strategy.
the compromise reached by mr kirkhope is based on strengthening the principles of non-discrimination, efficiency and transparency, all to the benefit of the ultimate beneficiary, the european citizen. first, both potential abuses against air carriers and potential interference by air carriers with the proper functioning of the agencies are prevented. secondly, transparency is ensured and consumer misinformation about flight selection, duration, operators and, not least, price is prevented, while also ensuring the protection of personal data. thirdly, beneficiaries are also given the option of rail transport for short-haul routes, which in the long run can bring environmental benefits by reducing carbon dioxide emissions. unfortunately, there are some issues that the code of conduct does not address, and they are not included in its scope. this is the pricing policy of low-cost companies, which do not cooperate with computerised reservation systems. i believe that the sound principles underlying this code of conduct should be adopted by all ticketing systems, including low-cost carriers. it is regrettable from the consumer's point of view that these companies are not themselves integrated into the crs. in addition to increasing the choice for passengers, this integration would also create positive pressure in terms of ensuring quality of service and price transparency. i therefore call on the european commission and the member states, through the competent bodies, to strengthen controls and to apply sanctions where appropriate, in order to ensure genuine consumer protection, for which companies not listed in the crs represent an accessible but misleading means of mobility. i also support and recommend the suggestion that in the future crs should consider introducing regular bus services into the systems.
the code of conduct for computerised reservation systems sets out the rules to be followed by air and rail transport operators when making reservations. the current situation shows that bookings made through the computerised reservation systems used by travel agencies lead to higher prices. i insist on the need to protect passengers' personal data. i believe that passengers should be able to choose the ticket that is most convenient for them and that, for this purpose, the passenger should be informed correctly and fully. i would stress the need for no discrimination between distribution channels or between passengers or travel agencies on the basis of their place of residence. certain distribution channels, such as the internet, respect the principle of non-discrimination, but computerised systems impose conditions on tour operators, which often lead to higher prices and discrimination based on the place of residence of passengers. i think this regulation is important, we must always keep the consumer in mind and i insist again on the protection of personal data.
as the fictitious rapporteur for the opinion on this file in the info committee on behalf of the epp-ed, i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done and on the report he has drawn up. i would like to stress the importance of this report in ensuring real competition in the area of computerised reservation systems. at the same time, we must not forget the rights of consumers and we must ensure that they benefit from the changes to this code of conduct. consumers should have all the details of the journey they wish to take. at the same time, it is very important that they know the exact price of tickets, so that they are not misled by any hidden costs. at the same time, i want to emphasize that what matters most is that the companies responsible for these sites no longer sit on the boards of directors, because they always have hidden costs. i would like to conclude by once again assuring the rapporteur of my full support for the vote in the chamber tomorrow.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on all the work and effort put into this document. maritime transport and ports are two key components of the chain linking the european single market to the world economy, being essential for handling 90% of europe's international trade. from the perspective of regional development, ports are one of the key elements of cohesion in europe, both because of the development of tourism capacity and because of the creation of over half a million jobs, which ensure both the dynamism and development of the outermost regions. in this context, aspects such as improving the image of ports and better integrating them into urban life, modernising them by exploiting the opportunities offered by the erdf and the cohesion funds, as well as involving local and port authorities in the management of water and air quality in ports, contribute significantly to regional development. an integrated approach is needed for a competitive european policy, linking economic, environmental, social and security aspects. the commission's communication on the future of the european union's external relations is a valuable contribution to the debate on the future of the union. finally, i would like to draw attention to the black sea ports which, although successfully fulfilling all the requirements of terminals, still need to be supplemented by ports and inland waterways to facilitate multimodal transport and trade with member states without access to the sea. in this respect, i believe that the danube represents a potential to be exploited with a view to establishing a logistical corridor linking the black sea area, the eastern gateway to europe, with western europe. the union should therefore pay particular attention to the black sea region, which can become a pole of growth and development for europe, thus helping to reduce disparities between the outermost and central regions.
some 30% of europe's freight movements take place in the ports of rotterdam, antwerp and hamburg, and 20% in the nine largest ports on the mediterranean. the accession of romania and bulgaria gives the union an outlet to the black sea and, by implication, direct access to important seaports such as constanta, mangalia, varna and burgas, as well as to the ports on the danube: galati, braila, tulcea and sulina. many european ports face differences in storage and loading/unloading capacities, poor terminal organisation, inefficient sea or land routes and access, long waiting times, insufficient security for trucks, trains and barges, low productivity and excessive, slow and costly formalities. it considers investment in new and improved facilities, waste treatment facilities, emission reductions, simplification of procedures, transparency of public financing, health and safety at work to be a priority. the structural funds, state aid, the naiades and marco polo programmes are just some of the community instruments available.
the union's economic development and competitiveness depend on efficient freight transport. we need to develop railway infrastructure, maritime corridors, port infrastructure and co-modality. improving connections between sea and river ports and the inland rail and road network is an important component of logistics infrastructure. the accession of romania and bulgaria gives the union an outlet to the black sea. the danube is now almost entirely an internal waterway of the union. this means new opportunities for european freight transport. i would stress, however, that efficient freight transport requires: balanced use of all modes of transport, traffic congestion reduction, simplification of procedures, legislative stability, investment in logistics systems and intelligent transport systems such as galileo, but above all, guaranteeing transport safety. programmes such as naiades and marco polo are not sufficiently used by member states to improve freight transport. i would like to draw the commission's attention to the barriers faced by some road hauliers, and i am referring to romanian road hauliers, when they transit through the territory of certain member states.
climate change is having a significant impact on human health, with the proliferation of certain infectious and parasitic diseases, caused in particular by the rise in temperature. frequent heat waves, floods, and fires on uncultivated land can lead to other diseases, poor hygiene, and death. romania is increasingly experiencing heat waves, floods and storms during the summer. this summer's floods have left thousands of romanian citizens without shelter and sanitation. i ask the commission to provide romania with appropriate financial support to mitigate the effects of these natural disasters. reducing emissions from transport, which account for 70% of urban pollution, will help improve air quality. directives such as fuel quality, reducing car emissions, promoting green vehicles for urban transport, will help reduce environmental pollution. however, it will be important to monitor their implementation and the effects achieved.
the international 'bio-initiative' report on electromagnetic fields and their effects on public health raises an alarm and finds that the existing limit values for protection against non-ionizing radiation are outdated and that immediate action is needed to reduce human exposure to radiation from equipment used by mobile phone operators. scientific studies have shown that this radiation causes health problems, such as sleep disturbances, childhood leukemia, significant increases in stress levels, and a ten-year increase in cell phone use that doubles the risk of brain cancer. the new action plan for health must take account of these threats, which are intensifying due to the emergence of new technologies and are gaining ground in rural areas and developing countries. further research is needed in this area and in mental health issues such as stress and depression to determine whether they may indeed be associated with non-ionizing radiation.

we thank all those who made it possible for a country in central and eastern europe to celebrate the year of creativity one year earlier, budapest being in fact the capital of this new european trend of creativity and innovation. we propose that, along the same lines, the top universities in scientific research should have the chance to promote european policy by organising, in at least one university in each of the two last waves, special events in which experts and specialists can have a say. we also propose that the first two or three researchers from each of the two waves take a tour of the top five universities and research centres in europe.
in writing. diversity is one of the sources of innovation, and the enlargement policy of the european union has brought new sources of diversity and therefore new sources of innovation to europe. unfortunately, however, for students from new entrants such as romania or bulgaria, the costs of participating in erasmus are still too high, which reduces their participation in the programme. in 1987, the erasmus programme was launched to provide students with european mobility and the opportunity to pursue a better career. after 21 years, the programme has not only succeeded in attracting 2 million students and 3100 higher education institutions, but has also actively contributed to improving students' academic life, intercultural skills and self-confidence. without explicitly aiming for this, the erasmus programme has succeeded in introducing students to the very essence of the european union: freedom of movement in this great family of diversity but unity. that is why, in the context of the year of innovation and creativity, i believe that an increase in the budget for students from the new member states would mean that they would be more involved in this programme and thus increase diversity as a source of innovation and creativity.
in writing. pluralism must be, we all agree, a vital element in media. as a vital element, it must be supported and, with the adoption of the mikko report, an important step has been taken in this direction. the need for a balanced media market must also be recognised and supported at member state level, with member states committing themselves, both separately and jointly, to providing european citizens with the opportunity to receive accurate and varied information. cultural diversity and the ever-growing need to integrate the migrant population and minorities, combined with the importance of good information for the working population, are the main reasons for creating a book on media freedom. in this respect, i strongly support the ep's recommendation to support public media services towards an alternative to information based solely on commercial criteria. the need for europe's citizens to actively exercise their rights and obligations, to be informed and able to understand and criticize the way they are informed, must guide any future action taken by both the european institutions and individual member states.
in writing. the timely implementation, correct transposition and correct application of internal market directives are fundamental conditions for the effective functioning of the internal market, consumer protection, with consequences for competitiveness and economic and social balance within the eu. the scoreboard is an important policy tool, in that it calls on the commission to further develop the range of information and indicators it contains, including quality, the social conditions of workers, and the impact on the environment and climate change. romania ranks 7th in the eu for the transposition of internal market directives, with an average transposition deficit of 0.8% in december 2007, compared to the 1% target set by the heads of state and government for 2009. the report also highlights that delays or incorrect application of european rules affect consumers and businesses and calls on member states to do more to promote the services of the solvit network (solvit is a problem-solving network, in which eu member states work together to resolve, without the use of legal procedures, problems arising from the incorrect application of internal market legislation by public authorities). i congratulate the reporter on her work.
in writing. – the report was based on the european commission’s communication ‘improving the quality of teacher education’ (sec(2007)0931) and stresses the need for the member states to reform the national education systems in order to improve teachers’ training. the rapporteur has pointed out some very important facts such as the difficulty of keeping the best candidates for the teaching profession, the low payment of teachers in many countries, the poor social status of teachers, teachers’ low level in foreign language learning and many more. in order to solve these problems, we should have a coherent, complex and complete strategy all over the eu. we should have more training programmes for teachers, and these programmes should be structured in such a way that the qualifications obtained in the end are recognised in all the member states. in order to achieve this, we need to share the responsibility with the national governments, as we may have the desire but they have the competence to reform the education system. i hope this report will be the first step in a long process that will end with a real improvement of the quality of teachers’ education across the european union.
