the current economic crisis requires extraordinary measures as more and more europeans face the spectre of unemployment and financial recession. raising the deposit guarantee ceiling for the general public is a welcome measure to preserve confidence in the banking system. an initial ceiling of €50,000 and then €100,000 is all the more appropriate for countries with a nontraditional banking system, such as romania and other former communist countries. at this point it is important that each state takes its own measure because otherwise there is a risk of panic among the population. romania is not among the countries with many deposits above eur 50 000. but psychologically speaking, raising the guaranteed amount can only produce positive effects considering that the deposits of the population decreased compared to september by 6 percent in bucharest alone. this means that some 600 million euros have been withdrawn in just a few weeks, a situation unprecedented in recent years. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year 2007-08.
mr president, the eu budget is being discussed at a time of rising anxiety regarding the economic crisis which is engulfing its member states. this crisis prompts the commission, the council and the european parliament to think about how the eu’s budgetary resources can combat the economic downturn. a considerably speedier disbursement of the structural funds in the new member states is essential under the new conditions, and the commission’s intention in this respect is more than welcome. however, this intention has to turn into concrete deeds, and the eu budget has to be ready in case additional payment appropriations are needed, as the report correctly highlights. incidentally, this hinges precisely on the simplification of procedures. for the non-euro-zone new member states, the leeway for using the budget stimulus out of their own resources is much reduced because of this financial crisis, and the credit crunch is likely to prevail on the international markets in 2009. therefore, eu funds and other forms of eu assistance within the framework of what i would call ‘credit enhancement’ are badly needed in order to fight the severe economic slowdown which is to be expected. donor countries might relish lower payments from the eu structural funds, with a view to the reorientation of these funds for other uses, but let us not deceive ourselves. if new member states get injured by this crisis more than their intrinsic weaknesses warrant, the effects would be bad for the union as a whole.
in writing. − the proposal for a directive is one of the most important elements of the climate change package, which sets a binding target of 20% for the share of renewable energy in eu energy consumption by 2020. the directive provides for the acquisition of new technologies, the creation of new jobs and the reduction of dependence on oil. the european parliament has played an important role in setting sustainability criteria for biofuels and social criteria which, in the context of the economic crisis, are very important for the citizens of the european union. climate change and energy insecurity are forcing us to promote new ways of creating energy without jeopardizing the availability of food. we need to ensure that the implementation of this directive will not endanger agricultural land or forests and that biofuels from raw materials grown on such land will not be taken into account in the incentives provided. the european union will once again show that it is a leader in promoting wind, solar, hydro and other alternative energy sources.
in writing. − we have supported from the outset the proposal to move from a 20% to 30% target automatically in the event of an international agreement being signed, and last week's negotiations led to a compromise which calls for the way to move to this level to be through a new procedure. this decision was taken as a precautionary measure to take into account the possibility of a future increase in the carbon price, but i am pleased to know that the 30% target will remain a priority to avoid an increase in average temperature of more than 2oc, as agreed at the march 2007 european council. an international agreement means a global effort to combat and adapt to climate change, and financial support to developing countries will provide an incentive for them to engage in efforts to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. to remain credible in its aid to developing countries, the european union must ensure that the funding of cdm projects will support sustainable development in these countries and that part of the revenues from the auctioning of emission credits is used to support them.
in writing. − promoting carbon capture and geological storage technologies will help to diversify energy efficiency and combat climate change. to reduce co2 emissions by 50% by 2050, the use of renewable energy is not sufficient to achieve this without also taking into account ccs projects. this will be a challenge for the european union, given the high capital investment costs of capture and storage equipment, which will however decrease as they are used on a large scale. for this reason, these demonstration projects are not mandatory as they depend heavily on the carbon price and technology. however, the eu has taken an important step towards finding alternative solutions to help reduce greenhouse gases, and the implementation of these projects in the future will stimulate other countries outside the eu to use these technologies.
in writing. − emissions from cars and their negative impact on the environment must not be neglected in the european union's efforts to combat the effects of climate change. the european parliament and the council agreed that from 2020 the new car fleet should achieve an average emission level of no more than 95g co2/km. the car industry has now committed itself to reducing its carbon dioxide emissions to 140g/km by 2008 under an agreement signed voluntarily in 1998. given the optional nature of this target, efforts to reduce emissions have been quite small, with a reduction from 186g/km in 1995 to only 163g/km in 2004. the new regulation introduces a mandatory co2 reduction scheme, a system of penalties for those who do not meet this target and incentives for the creation of innovative technologies. by 2014, 80% of the fleet will be compliant, and the penalty rate for every gram exceeded will be €95 after 2019. the final compromise ensures a balance between consumer needs, environmental protection and a sustainable industrial policy.
in writing. - i voted for mr sacconi's report on the emission performance standards for new cars. the road transport sector is responsible for around 70% of the greenhouse gas emissions produced by the transport sector. especially in urban areas, traffic congestion leads to air pollution in large urban agglomerations. it is therefore important to improve the emission performance standards for new cars. the compromise reached sets ambitious targets for car manufacturers, but also gives them the time needed to adapt production lines to the new requirements. the system of premiums introduced for green cars will provide an incentive for both producers and consumers. climate change will lead to both a change in consumer preferences and a revival in demand for cars. especially in the context of the economic and financial crisis, preserving jobs and creating the conditions for economic development are absolutely necessary. the importance of the automotive industry is also recognised by the special measures included in the european economic recovery programme.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive to facilitate the crossborder enforcement of road safety rules. 70% of road accidents are caused by speeding, not wearing a seatbelt, running a red light, or driving under the influence of alcohol. there are already bilateral agreements between some member states for cross-border prosecution of road safety infringements, but there is no common european framework yet. i would point out that the proposal for a directive only concerns financial sanctions. i believe that the commission's proposal will make a significant contribution to saving lives. it is regrettable that some 43 000 people, about the population of a medium-sized european city, die every year in europe as a result of road accidents. added to this are the 1.3 million people who die each year in road accidents. i regret that romania, with a rate of 13%, has recorded the highest increase in the number of road accidents in the last year. i hope that the majority vote in the european parliament will lead the council of the european union to speed up the adoption of the measures needed to reduce road accidents. to save human lives, we must not hesitate.

, in writing. under the charter of fundamental rights, every eu citizen is free to seek employment, work and settle in any other member state. unfortunately, not all european citizens have enjoyed this freedom. the two-year period of labour market restrictions imposed on new member states expires at the end of this year, but eight member states have already announced their intention to extend it for another three years in the context of the financial crisis. according to the commission report of 11.11.2008, there is no conclusive evidence that a significant number of local workers have lost their jobs or been affected by wage cuts due to workers coming from the new member states. keeping labour markets closed prolongs the differential treatment of european citizens. the lifting of these restrictions would help to avoid the problems arising from undeclared work or fictitious independent activities. i therefore believe that member states which still impose labour market restrictions should first take account of the reality of the positive impact that the free movement of workers has on sustainable economic growth. free movement has proved not only positive but necessary.
in writing. without commenting on the substance of this report, which is open to much criticism, i would like to draw attention to an article on which i will vote against - even though an amendment to delete it was rejected in the committee. this is paragraph 46, which recommends the formulation of a definition of national minorities at european level, referring to council of europe recommendation 1201 (1993). this recommendation should not be invoked without a very rigorous clarification of the interpretation given to it, as it contains ambiguous wording, which could be interpreted as granting collective rights to minorities or territorial autonomy on ethnic grounds. i believe that the european parliament should not accept a reference to this recommendation uncritically. even the venice commission - the european commission for democracy through law - has stressed that any interpretation of recommendation 1201 must be particularly cautious.

concerns and even my criticisms. frontex is an essential instrument in immigration policy and has proven its necessity and efficiency. however, it remains an overly-politicised body which is too dependent on member states’ goodwill and on national interests dictated by the press and public opinion. it was crucial to remind member states of their moral duty and commitment. it is also important to recall that frontex is a first-pillar community body. as such, it should not only respect the eu’s fundamental values in its activities, but also work for their promotion, particularly in a field which touches upon critical questions relating to migration and freedom of movement. however, the legality of its actions could be called into question. first of all because the coordinating intelligence-driven operations carried out by frontex are based on risk analyses and threat assessments conducted under the secrecy rule. this means little transparency and no democratic accountability. secondly, because the joint operation is coordinated by frontex, this creates an externalisation of the border which calls into question its compliance with the eu’s obligation of the principle of protection for asylum seekers and refugees. i therefore call for a comprehensive assessment and review of frontex’s operations and its accountability, involving parliament. i would also ask the commission to fully evaluate frontex’s activities with regard to their impact on fundamental freedoms and rights, including the responsibility to protect. finally, i believe the focus has so far been quite closely on maritime issues but, as mentioned, all the migration routes must be tackled. land routes will soon require close attention also, on the eastern borders, and for once we the introduction and use of new technologies in the judicial act to the greatest extent possible is essential. there's no way that justice can lag so far behind other areas. so a strategy in this regard must, of course, be taken very seriously. we must, however, look at the situation as it is, and keep our feet on the ground. in the 21st century, there are courts in the european union that do not have computers or internet access, as this report also highlights. regardless of the method of search, access to legal information is still very difficult, both for legal practitioners and, above all, for ordinary citizens seeking to defend their rights. i am convinced that the european funding programmes for civil justice, as well as for criminal justice, will provide more funds in the future to remedy these shortcomings. further efforts are also needed on the part of the member states to make efficient use of the funds currently available. the report on the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters, voted on two days ago, raises very similar issues. i am sorry that this report has not been debated. improving the way the network works is undoubtedly important and brings added value to european citizens. the same problems persist, however, as i mentioned earlier, namely the lack of information, the lack of translations into all the official languages, and the difficulty of accessing crossborder judicial documents. i thank you for your attention and i hope once again that these issues, which are a major concern of parliament, will be more prominently on the agenda of the commission and the council in the future, especially as citizens expect concrete measures from the european union to simplify their daily lives.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteurs, mrs diana wallis, mr manuel medina ortega and mr lópez-istúriz white, on their excellent reports. e-justice is a necessity given that the number of people involved in cross-border litigation in europe is estimated at 10 million and information technologies in justice could significantly contribute to improving the accessibility and efficiency of the european legal and judicial system. that is why mrs. wallis' report and her efforts deserve our full consideration. i am also convinced of the particular importance of the resolution on the authentic instrument. as a lawyer from romania, i cannot help but point out that the benefits of the authentic act and of graceful, non-contentious justice are very great. the most important form in which preventive justice is manifested in romania, as in european civil law countries, is the authentic notarial act. i understand that mr. medina ortega wishes to refer exclusively to authentic documents and to make a distinction between authentic public documents, issued exclusively by a specialized professional, delegated by public authority, and those under private signature, on the other hand. however, regardless of the outcome of the debate and whether equivalent instruments will be included or will be the role of another initiative, i believe that this report must ensure, have the objective of ensuring, the protection of the citizen and his legal security, cross-border family and property relations, by proposing the mutual recognition of authentic instruments.
i welcome the initiative on the circulation of authentic instruments throughout europe, as it will contribute to the development of the free movement of persons and business entities in the european union. although physical borders have been abolished, legal ones persist, as evidenced by the complex procedures, varying from one state to another, for enforcing contracts concluded before a representative of the public authority. it is our duty to give every citizen the possibility of being covered by the provisions of a european authentic instrument drawn up in one member state in another member state of the european union without any further procedures. i welcome the initiative and the report by mrs wallis on e-justice, as i believe that the adoption of this report will ensure that european citizens have access to the european legal and judicial system through the use of information and communication technology. the rapid administration of evidence at minimal cost and the simplification of judicial procedures through simple and useful tools will facilitate citizens' access to justice in cross-border disputes. for touching these...

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because labour mobility is a fundamental right conferred by the treaty on eu citizens, and thus becomes one of the main pillars of the european social model through which the objectives of the lisbon strategy can be achieved. i welcome the report because, in addition to drawing attention to the obstacles to the free movement of workers from the new member states on the labour market, it brings important elements to the european action plan on labour mobility presented by the european commission, such as support for programmes linking education and the labour market, mutual recognition of diplomas and the expansion of the eures network.
in writing. − there is no better justification than the presentation of concrete data: the romanian press has just today presented the results of a control carried out by the romanian consumer protection office. the inspectors found that 90% of the toys checked had deviations during a recent inspection. some toys did not have instructions for use and were not age-appropriate. inspectors also found toy pistols and swords that were considered dangerous. other toys had small parts that could be easily detached. according to the results of this audit, china remains the main source of dangerous toys and yet remains the main supplier to the european union. in the interest of our children, drastic measures are needed in this regard.
in writing. − vocational education and training is a subject which has gained particular importance in recent years. the introduction of a european credit system in vocational education and training will contribute to the development and expansion of european cooperation in the field of education. it also leads to improved mobility and portability of qualifications at national level, both between different sectors of the economy and within the labour market. vocational education and training is crucial in europe's efforts to respond to the social challenges posed by ageing societies, to reposition itself in the global economy and to resolve the economic crisis. i therefore consider it important that member states validate non-formal and informal education, especially as the number of graduates in vocational education and training will fall sharply between 2009 and 2015, but at the same time the need for vocationally qualified staff to fill vacancies on the labour market will increase significantly. i therefore believe it is particularly important that european bodies actively support partnerships between member states and european companies in this area a cost-sharing system.
in writing. − the commission's drive to stimulate the simplification and harmonisation of eu company law with the aim of reducing the administrative burden by 25% by 2012 is a prerequisite for making european companies more efficient and making the community business environment more attractive, generating savings estimated at eur 150 billion. the initiative to revise the regulations contained in the fourth and seventh company law directives to exempt not only small but also medium-sized enterprises or parent enterprises with subsidiaries considered insignificant from the obligations to present financial and accounting information and to draw up consolidated accounts has the rapporteur's input and support, ensuring in the future the stability and certainty of an appropriate legal framework for a segment that plays a major role in generating jobs in the union. i also welcome the emphasis by the rapporteur on the need for transparency and fair information for all stakeholders, in particular through the widespread implementation of information and communication technology-based financial reporting systems.
